guia-calculadora-super-solo.excerptEn: Learn how to calculate ingredient proportions to build organic super soil at any volume.
guia-calculadora-super-solo.excerptEs: Aprende a calcular las proporciones de ingredientes para preparar súper sustrato orgánico en cualquier volumen.
guia-calculadora-super-solo.contentEn:
## Objective

Build **organic super soil** with quantities in grams and ml — selecting only the components you intend to use.

## When to use it

- When preparing substrate from scratch or replenishing a batch
- To make a shopping list before mixing
- When you do not have every input available (uncheck what is missing)

## Step by step

1. Enter the **total substrate volume** in liters (e.g., 45 L)
2. Check the **components** you will add (bokashi, worm castings, castor cake, etc.)
3. Click **Calculate Ingredients** in the [Super Soil Calculator](/calculadoras/super-solo.html)
4. Write down the grams and ml for each selected item

## Available components

- **Bokashi** (10 g/L) — biological activator
- **Worm Castings** (15 g/L) — organic matter and microbiota
- **Castor Cake**, **Bone Meal**, **Rock Dust**, **Biochar**, **Gypsum**, **Dolomitic Lime**, **Neem Cake**, **Kelp Meal**

With **all** components selected: 61 g/L. The total shown in the result depends only on what you select.

## Tips

- Use **Select all** / **Clear all** to test lean recipes
- Mix dry amendments before moistening
- Let the soil cure for 2–4 weeks before planting

---

🧮 [Open Super Soil Calculator](/calculadoras/super-solo.html)
guia-calculadora-super-solo.contentEs:
## Objetivo

Preparar **súper sustrato orgánico** con dosis en gramos y ml, seleccionando solo los componentes que vas a usar.

## Cuándo usarlo

- Al preparar sustrato desde cero o reponer un lote
- Para armar una lista de compras antes de mezclar
- Cuando no cuentes con todos los insumos (desmarca lo que falte)

## Paso a paso

1. Ingresa el **volumen total de sustrato** en litros (p. ej., 45 L)
2. Marca los **componentes** que vas a agregar (bokashi, humus de lombriz, torta de ricino, etc.)
3. Haz clic en **Calcular ingredientes** en la [Calculadora de Súper Sustrato](/calculadoras/super-solo.html)
4. Anota los gramos y ml de cada elemento seleccionado

## Componentes disponibles

- **Bokashi** (10 g/L) — activador biológico
- **Humus de Lombriz** (15 g/L) — materia orgánica y microbiota
- **Torta de Ricino**, **Harina de Hueso**, **Polvo de Roca**, **Biochar**, **Yeso**, **Cal Dolomítica**, **Torta de Neem**, **Harina de Algas**

Con **todos** los componentes marcados: 61 g/L. El total del resultado depende solo de lo que selecciones.

## Consejos

- Usa **Marcar todos** / **Desmarcar todos** para probar recetas simples
- Mezcla las enmiendas secas antes de humedecer
- Deja curar el sustrato durante 2–4 semanas antes de plantar

guia-calculadora-luximetro.excerptEn: How to measure PPFD and lux with your phone camera — calibration, positioning, and reliable readings.
guia-calculadora-luximetro.excerptEs: Cómo medir PPFD y lux con la cámara del celular: calibración, posicionamiento y lecturas confiables.
guia-calculadora-luximetro.contentEn:
## Objective

Learn how to use the website's **Lux Meter (Camera)** to estimate PPFD and lux at the plant canopy.

## When to use it

- When setting up or repositioning grow lights
- To compare intensity across tent corners
- Before calculating DLI (record the average PPFD)

## Step by step

1. Open the [Lux Meter](/calculadoras/luximetro.html) on your phone and allow camera access
2. Tap **Start Camera** and point it at the measurement point (canopy height)
3. Select the corresponding **light type** (grow LED, HPS, sunlight, etc.)
4. Center the bright area in the measurement circle and wait for the reading to stabilize
5. Record the displayed PPFD (μmol/m²/s) and lux values

## How to interpret it

- The status badge indicates whether intensity is low, appropriate, or excessive for the growth stage
- PPFD is more useful than lux for comparing different light types
- Take 3 readings at different points and use the average

## Tips

- Avoid shadows from your body or phone over the measured area
- Clean the camera lens before measuring
- Treat it as an estimate — validate with a dedicated lux meter whenever possible

---

🧮 [Open Lux Meter](/calculadoras/luximetro.html)
guia-calculadora-luximetro.contentEs:
## Objetivo

Aprende a usar el **Luxómetro (Cámara)** del sitio para estimar PPFD y lux en el dosel de las plantas.

## Cuándo usarlo

- Al instalar o reposicionar luminarias
- Para comparar la intensidad entre las esquinas de la carpa
- Antes de calcular el DLI (anota el PPFD promedio)

## Paso a paso

1. Abre el [Luxómetro](/calculadoras/luximetro.html) en el celular y permite el acceso a la cámara
2. Toca **Iniciar cámara** y apunta al punto de medición (altura del dosel)
3. Selecciona el **tipo de luz** correspondiente (LED de cultivo, HPS, solar, etc.)
4. Centra el área luminosa en el círculo de medición y espera a que la lectura se estabilice
5. Anota los valores de PPFD (μmol/m²/s) y lux mostrados

## Cómo interpretarlo

- La etiqueta de estado indica si la intensidad es baja, adecuada o excesiva para la etapa
- El PPFD es más útil que los lux para comparar distintos tipos de luz
- Haz 3 lecturas en puntos diferentes y usa el promedio

## Consejos

- Evita las sombras de tu cuerpo o del celular sobre el área medida
- Limpia la lente de la cámara antes de medir
- Tómalo como una estimación; valida con un luxómetro dedicado siempre que sea posible

---

otimizacao-propagacao-vegetal.excerptEn: A seed-starting and cloning protocol using biodegradable pots and rigorous microclimate control.
otimizacao-propagacao-vegetal.excerptEs: Protocolo de siembra y clonación con macetas biodegradables y control microclimático riguroso.
otimizacao-propagacao-vegetal.contentEn:
## Summary

This study documents a seed-starting and vegetative-cloning protocol using biodegradable containers made from recycled cellulose, integrated with microclimate control in a **Mars Hydro** unit.

## Introduction

Transplant shock limits the early vigor of seedlings. Pots that decompose *in situ* reduce root damage during the critical establishment phase.

## Methodology

- Seed soaking in an aqueous medium (24 h)
- Germination in moist cellulose paper, zero photoperiod (24 h)
- Cylindrical pots made of recycled printer paper with aeration holes
- Monitoring PPFD, CO₂, and temperature in the experimental tent

## Results

Emerging radicles were positioned orthotropically; continuous development occurred **without classic post-transplant stress signs** during the first two weeks.

## Conclusion

A viable small-scale propagation method that combines sustainability with state-of-the-art technological control.

---

📄 Read the full report at [Research: Substrates](/biblioteca/pesquisas/substratos.html).

![](/uploads/icon-192-1782543515824.png)
otimizacao-propagacao-vegetal.contentEs:
## Resumen

Este estudio documenta el protocolo de siembra y clonación vegetativa mediante recipientes biodegradables elaborados con celulosa reciclada, integrado al control microclimático de una unidad **Mars Hydro**.

## Introducción

El estrés del trasplante limita el vigor inicial de las plántulas. Las macetas que se descomponen *in situ* reducen el daño radicular en el momento crítico del establecimiento.

## Metodología

- Remojo de las semillas en medio acuoso (24 h)
- Germinación en papel de celulosa húmedo, fotoperiodo cero (24 h)
- Macetas cilíndricas de papel sulfito reciclado con orificios de aireación
- Monitoreo de PPFD, CO₂ y temperatura en la carpa experimental

## Resultados

Radículas emergentes posicionadas ortotrópicamente; desarrollo continuo **sin signos clásicos de estrés posterior al trasplante** durante las primeras dos semanas.

## Conclusión

Metodología viable para la propagación a pequeña escala, que combina sostenibilidad y control tecnológico de vanguardia.

---

📄 Lee el informe completo en [Investigación: Sustratos](/biblioteca/pesquisas/substratos.html).

inspecao-ventilacao-tenda.titleEs: Inspección: Sistema de Ventilación de la Carpa
inspecao-ventilacao-tenda.excerptEn: Assessment of airflow, noise, and thermal exchange in the lab's exhaust duct and carbon filter.
inspecao-ventilacao-tenda.excerptEs: Verificación del flujo de aire, ruido e intercambio térmico en el conducto de extracción y filtro de carbón del laboratorio.
inspecao-ventilacao-tenda.contentEn:
## Scope

Inspection of the main tent's **ventilation system**: inline exhaust fan, carbon filter, flexible duct, and passive intakes.

## Measurements

| Point | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Exhaust fan noise (1 m) | 46 dB |
| Tent ΔT vs. room | +2.5 °C |
| Estimated air exchanges | ~1.2 min⁻¹ |

## Findings

- A sharp duct bend reduces airflow by ~15%
- A saturated filter raises noise by 4 dB compared with a new filter
- The lower passive intake balances negative pressure

## Recommendations

1. Replace the filter every 6–9 months of continuous use
2. Shorten the duct or use wide-radius elbows
3. Document a quarterly review on the channel

## Status

**Approved** — system suitable for the tent's current volume.
inspecao-ventilacao-tenda.contentEs:
## Alcance

Inspección del **sistema de ventilación** de la carpa principal: extractor en línea, filtro de carbón, conducto flexible y entradas pasivas.

## Mediciones

| Punto | Valor |
|-------|-------|
| Ruido del extractor (1 m) | 46 dB |
| ΔT de la carpa frente al ambiente | +2,5 °C |
| Renovaciones estimadas | ~1,2 min⁻¹ |

## Hallazgos

- Un codo pronunciado en el conducto reduce el flujo ~15%
- Un filtro saturado aumenta el ruido en 4 dB frente a un filtro nuevo
- La entrada pasiva inferior equilibra la presión negativa

## Recomendaciones

1. Sustituir el filtro cada 6–9 meses de uso continuo
2. Acortar el conducto o usar codos de radio amplio
3. Documentar una revisión trimestral en el canal

## Estado

**Aprobado** — sistema adecuado para el volumen actual de la carpa.

clonadora-aeroponica-documentada.titleEn: DIY Cloner: Ice Cream Tub Build
clonadora-aeroponica-documentada.titleEs: Clonadora Casera: Montaje con Pote de Helado
clonadora-aeroponica-documentada.excerptEn: A simple cloner made from an ice cream tub, kitchen sponges, and a 24-hour pump — up to 6 cuttings at low cost.
clonadora-aeroponica-documentada.excerptEs: Clonadora simple con un pote de helado, esponjas de cocina y una bomba funcionando 24 horas: hasta 6 esquejes a bajo costo.
clonadora-aeroponica-documentada.contentEn:
## Objective

Document Inspector BudGanja's DIY cloner: an **ice cream tub**, **6 holes in the lid**, holders made from **kitchen sponges**, and an **aquarium pump running 24 h** until roots emerge.

## Materials

- 1 ice cream tub with lid
- 1 aquarium pump
- Kitchen sponges (6 cut rounds)
- Clean water

## Assembly summary

1. Drill 6 round holes in the lid
2. Cut 6 sponge rounds and slit each one to hold the cutting
3. Fit the sponges into the holes, place cuttings in the sponge, and set the lid on the water-filled tub
4. Keep the pump on **24/7** — no timer

## Lab results

Observed rooting rate: **78%** in 14 days in previous tests with continuous oxygenation.

---

🛠️ Complete manual: [DIY Cloner](/equipamentos/manual-clonadora.html).
clonadora-aeroponica-documentada.contentEs:
## Objetivo

Documentar la clonadora casera del Inspector BudGanja: **pote de helado**, **6 orificios en la tapa**, soporte con **esponjas de cocina** y una **bomba de acuario encendida 24 h** hasta que salgan las raíces.

## Materiales

- 1 pote de helado con tapa
- 1 bomba de acuario
- Esponjas de cocina (6 círculos cortados)
- Agua limpia

## Resumen del montaje

1. Haz 6 orificios redondos en la tapa
2. Corta 6 círculos de esponja y ábrelos por la mitad para sujetar el esqueje
3. Coloca las esponjas en los orificios, los esquejes en la esponja y la tapa sobre el pote con agua
4. Mantén la bomba encendida **24/7** — sin temporizador

## Resultados del laboratorio

Tasa de enraizamiento observada: **78%** en 14 días en pruebas anteriores con oxigenación continua.

---

🛠️ Manual completo: [Clonadora Casera](/equipamentos/manual-clonadora.html).

inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicina.titleEn: Inspection: UNIFESP Course — Medicinal Cannabis sativa L.
inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicina.titleEs: Inspección: Curso UNIFESP — Cannabis sativa L. medicinal
inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicina.excerptEn: Audit of UNIFESP's 14th extension course with MovReCam — 10,000 free places, 57 hours of YouTube-based distance learning, a 75% attendance certificate, and clinical, legal, and cultivation modules.
inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicina.excerptEs: Auditoría del XIV curso de extensión de UNIFESP junto con MovReCam: 10.000 plazas gratuitas, 57 h de educación a distancia por YouTube, certificado con 75% de asistencia y módulos clínicos, legales y de cultivo.
inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicina.contentEn:
## Scope

Documentary inspection of the **14th Course on the therapeutic use of Cannabis sativa L.**, a university **extension course** offered by the Federal University of São Paulo (UNIFESP) in partnership with the **Movement for Cannabis Regulation (MovReCam)**. The program has been offered since 2018, with more than **100,000 cumulative participants** across prior editions, and received the **CannaPortugal Global Cannabis Awards 2025** as a benchmark for democratic cannabis education.

> **Methodological note:** independent editorial audit by Inspector BudGanja based on the official **SIEX/PROEC** catalog (code 30063), the public teaching plan, and UNIFESP institutional notices. **No affiliation** with the university or MovReCam; deadlines, vacancies, and certificate rules may be updated — always confirm on [SIEX](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/30063/mais-info) before enrolling.

## Inspected subject

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Institution | [UNIFESP](https://www.unifesp.br/) — Federal University of São Paulo |
| SIEX action | Code **30063** · Base year **2026** |
| Official title | 14th Course on the therapeutic use of Cannabis sativa L. |
| Type | Extension course · Continuing education · **Health** area |
| Partnership | MovReCam ([youtube.com/movrecam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam)) |
| Coordination (RTC) | Prof. Dr. **Eliana Rodrigues** |
| Deputy coordination | Luciana Togni de Lima Surjus · Gabrielle Dainezi (external) |
| Places | **10,000** |
| Format | Distance learning — classes on YouTube |
| Workload | **57 h** of theory (no mandatory in-person practice) |
| Period (14th edition) | **06/16/2026** to **11/12/2026** |
| Enrollment (14th edition) | **06/03/2026** to **06/30/2026** |
| Schedule | Tuesdays and Thursdays, from **7:30 p.m.** (except national holidays) |
| Prerequisite | At least **18 years old** |
| Fees | Enrollment and certificate **free** |
| Certificate | ≥ **75%** attendance · issued by the student in SIEX within 30 days after the final class |
| Contact | [curso.cannabismedicinal@unifesp.br](mailto:curso.cannabismedicinal@unifesp.br) |
| Inspection date | 2026-06-30 |

## Hypotheses and method

- **H1:** A free and open federal course reduces barriers to information on medicinal cannabis for patients, families, and health professionals.
- **H2:** YouTube broadcasts with attendance forms balance scale (10,000 places) and minimum traceability for certification.
- **H3:** The interdisciplinary curriculum — botany, pharmacology, clinical practice, legislation, and cultivation — aligns with what the BudGanja lab documents in [cultivation inspections](/biblioteca/inspecoes/) and [calculators](/calculadoras/), but with a **therapeutic and regulatory** focus rather than agronomic yield.
- **Method:** (1) review of SIEX 30063 and the teaching plan; (2) thematic mapping of the 42 scheduled classes; (3) cross-reference with Inspector BudGanja content (indoor environment, propagation, nutrition); (4) verification of certificate requirements and official channels.

## Curriculum structure (14th edition)

The teaching plan organizes the course into progressive blocks — from the scientific foundation to clinical applications, legislation, and production techniques:

| Block | Main topics (sample from the official curriculum) |
|-------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Fundamentals** | History and prohibitionism · Botany · Ethnobotany · Phytotherapy |
| **System and pharmacology** | SUS and cannabis · Living pharmacy · Endocannabinoidome · Cannabimimetics · Chemical composition and chemotypes |
| **Clinical practice by condition** | Epilepsy · ASD · Parkinson's · Alzheimer's · pain/fibromyalgia · cancer and palliative care · anxiety · sleep · women's health · veterinary care · harm reduction |
| **Clinical care practice** | Prescribing, dosing, and titration · Nursing · Adverse reactions · Drug interactions |
| **Policy and market** | Brazilian and comparative legislation · Social movements · Associations · Domestic and international market |
| **Production and technique** | Planting, organic cultivation, and cloning (2 classes) · Extraction methods |

### Findings — teaching and access

1. **Genuine democratization** — no selection process, no tuition, and a broad target audience (no degree required). It arose from community demand (an origin connected to Padre Ticão and Prof. **Elisaldo Carlini**, according to the [UNIFESP portal](https://portal.unifesp.br/destaques/curso-sobre-cannabis-medicinal-da-unifesp-e-movrecam-ganha-premio-internacional)).
2. **Trackable asynchronous attendance** — every class provides **Google Forms** using the **same enrollment email**; students should keep proof of submission (screenshots). Classes remain on YouTube for later reference.
3. **Dense clinical curriculum** — broad specialty coverage; useful as a study map, but not a substitute for a hospital protocol or medical residency.
4. **Cultivation modules** — partially align with the lab's [Inspections](/biblioteca/inspecoes/) and [propagation/cloning](/equipamentos/clonadora-6-estacas.html), but **without environmental metrics** (PPFD, VPD, EC) required in our journal.

### Findings — certification and limits

| Criterion | Official rule | Implication |
|----------|---------------|-------------|
| Minimum attendance | 75% of classes | Individual control; forms for each session |
| Issuance | By the student in [SIEX](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex) → “consult enrollment” | Deadline: up to 30 days after the final class |
| Certificate nature | UNIFESP university extension | **Does not** equal a degree or automatic professional qualification — verify with your professional board or employer |
| Curriculum changes | Class order may change according to speakers | Final content preserved, according to SIEX |

## Complementarity with Inspector BudGanja

| UNIFESP course topic | BudGanja resource |
|---------------------|-------------------|
| Botany, chemotypes, extraction | [Inspections](/biblioteca/inspecoes/) · [Research](/biblioteca/pesquisas/) |
| Broadcast and video archive | [YouTube MovReCam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam) |
| Planting, cloning, organic cultivation | [Propagation and cloning](/equipamentos/clonadora-6-estacas.html) · [Research journal](/cultivo/) |
| Indoor environment (not central to the course) | [Indoor PPFD](/calculadoras/luximetro.html) · [Lux Meter Calculator](/calculadoras/luximetro.html) · [VPD](/calculadoras/cultivo-lab.html?mode=vpd) |
| Nutrition and substrate | [Nutrition](/calculadoras/cultivo-lab.html?mode=ec) · [Living soil](/calculadoras/super-solo.html) |
| Brazilian legislation and market | [Mars Hydro Inspection](/posts/post-inspecao-marshydro-brasil.html) (commercial catalog) · [YouTube MovReCam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam) (advocacy) |

## How to participate (14th edition)

1. **Enrollment** — [SIEX 30063](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/30063/inscricao-acao/inscrever) (within the published deadline).
2. **Classes** — [YouTube MovReCam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam), Tuesdays and Thursdays at 7:30 p.m.
3. **Attendance** — complete each class form with your name, email, and CPF (email must match your enrollment).
4. **Certificate** — after ≥75% attendance, issue it in [consult enrollment](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex) ([PROEC instructions](https://www.unifesp.br/reitoria/proec/consultar-)).

## Credits and transparency

- **Course, curriculum, and certificates** © UNIFESP / PROEC — [siex.siiu.unifesp.br](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/30063/mais-info)
- **Broadcast and video archive** © MovReCam — [youtube.com/movrecam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam)
- **Inspection written by:** Inspector BudGanja (independent digital laboratory)
- **Purpose:** guide growers and people seeking education — **not** an institutional endorsement or a guarantee of a place

## Status

**Approved as a public-education reference** — Brazil's largest free university-extension program on medicinal cannabis, with a robust clinical curriculum, open access, and a federal certificate. It is recommended to pair the cultivation modules with real measurements in the [BudGanja laboratory](/cultivo/) and to validate the certificate according to your professional field.

[▶ SIEX enrollment (14th edition)](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/30063/inscricao-acao/inscrever) · [Teaching plan](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/plano-ensino/30063) · [All inspections](/biblioteca/inspecoes/)
inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicina.contentEs:
## Alcance

Inspección documental del **XIV Curso sobre el uso terapéutico de Cannabis sativa L.**, un curso de **extensión universitaria** de la Universidad Federal de São Paulo (UNIFESP), en alianza con el **Movimiento por la Regulación del Cannabis (MovReCam)**. El programa se ofrece desde 2018, con más de **100.000 participantes** acumulados en las ediciones anteriores, y recibió los **CannaPortugal Global Cannabis Awards 2025** como referencia de educación democrática sobre cannabis.

> **Nota metodológica:** auditoría editorial independiente del Inspector BudGanja basada en el catálogo oficial **SIEX/PROEC** (código 30063), el plan de enseñanza público y comunicados institucionales de UNIFESP. **Sin vínculo** con la universidad ni MovReCam; los plazos, cupos y reglas del certificado pueden actualizarse — confirma siempre en [SIEX](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/30063/mais-info) antes de inscribirte.

## Objeto inspeccionado

| Campo | Valor |
|-------|-------|
| Institución | [UNIFESP](https://www.unifesp.br/) — Universidad Federal de São Paulo |
| Acción SIEX | Código **30063** · Año base **2026** |
| Título oficial | XIV Curso sobre el uso terapéutico de Cannabis sativa L. |
| Tipo | Curso de extensión · Educación continua · Área de **Salud** |
| Alianza | MovReCam ([youtube.com/movrecam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam)) |
| Coordinación (RTC) | Profa. Dra. **Eliana Rodrigues** |
| Vicecoordinación | Luciana Togni de Lima Surjus · Gabrielle Dainezi (externa) |
| Cupos | **10.000** |
| Modalidad | A distancia — clases en YouTube |
| Carga horaria | **57 h** teóricas (sin práctica presencial obligatoria) |
| Período (XIV) | **16/06/2026** al **12/11/2026** |
| Inscripciones (XIV) | **03/06/2026** al **30/06/2026** |
| Horario | Martes y jueves, a partir de las **19:30** (excepto feriados nacionales) |
| Requisito | Ser mayor de **18 años** |
| Tasas | Inscripción y certificado **gratuitos** |
| Certificado | ≥ **75%** de asistencia · emitido por el estudiante en SIEX hasta 30 días después de la última clase |
| Contacto | [curso.cannabismedicinal@unifesp.br](mailto:curso.cannabismedicinal@unifesp.br) |
| Fecha de la inspección | 2026-06-30 |

## Hipótesis y método

- **H1:** Un curso federal gratuito y abierto reduce las barreras de acceso a información sobre cannabis medicinal para pacientes, familiares y profesionales de la salud.
- **H2:** Las transmisiones por YouTube con formularios de asistencia equilibran la escala (10.000 cupos) y la trazabilidad mínima para la certificación.
- **H3:** La malla interdisciplinaria — botánica, farmacología, clínica, legislación y cultivo — se aproxima a lo que el laboratorio BudGanja documenta en [inspecciones de cultivo](/biblioteca/inspecoes/) y [calculadoras](/calculadoras/), pero con enfoque **terapéutico y regulatorio**, no de rendimiento agronómico.
- **Método:** (1) lectura de la ficha SIEX 30063 y del plan de enseñanza; (2) mapeo temático de las 42 clases programadas; (3) cruce con contenidos del Inspector BudGanja (ambiente indoor, propagación, nutrición); (4) verificación de requisitos de certificado y canales oficiales.

## Estructura de la malla (XIV edición)

El plan de enseñanza organiza el recorrido en bloques progresivos, desde la base científica hasta las aplicaciones clínicas, la legislación y las técnicas de producción:

| Bloque | Temas principales (muestra de la malla oficial) |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------|
| **Fundamentos** | Historia y prohibicionismo · Botánica · Etnobotánica · Fitoterapia |
| **Sistema y farmacología** | SUS y cannabis · Farmacia viva · Endocannabinoidoma · Cannabimiméticos · Composición química y quimiotipos |
| **Clínica por patología** | Epilepsia · TEA · Parkinson · Alzheimer · dolor/fibromialgia · cáncer y cuidados paliativos · ansiedad · sueño · salud de la mujer · veterinaria · reducción de daños |
| **Práctica asistencial** | Prescripción, dosificación y titulación · Enfermería · Reacciones adversas · Interacciones medicamentosas |
| **Política y mercado** | Legislación brasileña y comparada · Movimientos sociales · Asociativismo · Mercado nacional e internacional |
| **Producción y técnica** | Siembra, cultivo orgánico y clonación (2 clases) · Métodos de extracción |

### Hallazgos — pedagogía y acceso

1. **Democratización real** — sin proceso de selección, sin matrícula y con público objetivo amplio (no exige título universitario). Nació de una demanda comunitaria (origen vinculado al Padre Ticão y al prof. **Elisaldo Carlini**, según el [portal de UNIFESP](https://portal.unifesp.br/destaques/curso-sobre-cannabis-medicinal-da-unifesp-e-movrecam-ganha-premio-internacional)).
2. **Asistencia asincrónica trazable** — cada clase ofrece **Google Forms** con el **mismo correo de inscripción**; el estudiante debe guardar comprobantes (capturas). Las clases permanecen en YouTube para consulta posterior.
3. **Malla clínica sólida** — amplia cobertura de especialidades; útil como mapa de estudio, pero no sustituye un protocolo hospitalario ni una residencia médica.
4. **Módulos de cultivo** — se alinean parcialmente con las [Inspecciones](/biblioteca/inspecoes/) y la [propagación/clonación](/equipamentos/clonadora-6-estacas.html) del laboratorio, pero **sin métricas ambientales** (PPFD, VPD, EC) exigidas en nuestro diario.

### Hallazgos — certificación y límites

| Criterio | Regla oficial | Implicación |
|----------|---------------|-------------|
| Asistencia mínima | 75% de las clases | Control individual; formularios por encuentro |
| Emisión | Por el propio estudiante en [SIEX](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex) → «consultar inscripción» | Plazo: hasta 30 días después de la última clase |
| Naturaleza del certificado | Extensión universitaria UNIFESP | **No** equivale a un título ni a habilitación profesional automática — valida con tu colegio profesional o empleador |
| Cambios en la malla | El orden de las clases puede cambiar según los ponentes | Contenido final preservado, según SIEX |

## Complementariedad con el Inspector BudGanja

| Tema del curso UNIFESP | Recurso BudGanja |
|------------------------|------------------|
| Botánica, quimiotipos, extracción | [Inspecciones](/biblioteca/inspecoes/) · [Investigaciones](/biblioteca/pesquisas/) |
| Transmisión y archivo de video | [YouTube MovReCam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam) |
| Siembra, clonación, cultivo orgánico | [Propagación y clonación](/equipamentos/clonadora-6-estacas.html) · [Diario de investigaciones](/cultivo/) |
| Ambiente indoor (no central en el curso) | [PPFD indoor](/calculadoras/luximetro.html) · [Calculadora Luxómetro](/calculadoras/luximetro.html) · [VPD](/calculadoras/cultivo-lab.html?mode=vpd) |
| Nutrición y sustrato | [Nutrición](/calculadoras/cultivo-lab.html?mode=ec) · [Suelo vivo](/calculadoras/super-solo.html) |
| Legislación y mercado BR | [Inspección Mars Hydro](/posts/post-inspecao-marshydro-brasil.html) (catálogo comercial) · [YouTube MovReCam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam) (incidencia) |

## Cómo participar (XIV edición)

1. **Inscripción** — [SIEX 30063](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/30063/inscricao-acao/inscrever) (dentro del plazo publicado).
2. **Clases** — [YouTube MovReCam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam), martes y jueves a las 19:30.
3. **Asistencia** — completa el formulario de cada clase con nombre, correo electrónico y CPF (el correo debe ser el mismo de la inscripción).
4. **Certificado** — después de ≥75% de asistencia, emítelo en [consultar inscripción](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex) (instrucciones [PROEC](https://www.unifesp.br/reitoria/proec/consultar-)).

## Créditos y transparencia

- **Curso, malla y certificados** © UNIFESP / PROEC — [siex.siiu.unifesp.br](https://siex.siiu.unifesp.br/catalogo-siex/30063/mais-info)
- **Transmisión y archivo de video** © MovReCam — [youtube.com/movrecam](https://www.youtube.com/movrecam)
- **Inspección redactada por:** Inspector BudGanja (laboratorio digital independiente)
- **Finalidad:** orientar a cultivadores y personas interesadas en formación — **no** constituye respaldo institucional ni garantía de cupo

## Estado

**Aprobado como referencia de formación pública** — el mayor programa gratuito de extensión universitaria sobre cannabis medicinal en Brasil, con una malla clínica robusta, acceso abierto y certificado federal. Se recomienda cruzar los módulos de cultivo con mediciones reales en el [laboratorio BudGanja](/cultivo/) y validar el certificado según tu campo profesional.

inspecao-planta-babosa.contentEn:
## Scope

Educational inspection of **Aloe** (*Aloe vera*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/plantas/babosa/](/plantas/babosa/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Aloe** |
| Scientific name | *Aloe vera* |
| Family | Asphodelaceae |
| Catalog slug | `babosa` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

Succulent (*Aloe vera*) widely grown; leaf gel rich in polysaccharides — topical tradition; latex with anthraquinones (aloin) needs caution if ingested.

## Parts used

- Leaves (gel)

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Topical gel on irritated skin and mild burns (folk tradition)
- Homemade cosmetics (masks, moisturizing)
- Internal use only with guidance — distinct from external gel

## Cautions

Separate inner leaf gel from yellow latex (aloin / anthraquinones). Internal use and concentrated extracts need professional guidance; latex may irritate. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Identity and etymology

The Portuguese **babosa** names the viscous gel; **Aloe vera** comes from Latin *aloe* (bitter plant) and *vera* (true). Do not confuse with other *Aloe* species with different chemistry.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Polysaccharides (acemannan) | Inner leaf gel — hydrating mucilage; marker often cited in studies of purified gel. |
| Anthraquinones (aloin / barbaloin) | Concentrated mainly in yellow peripheral latex — laxative effect; separate gel from latex in home prep. |
| Phenolic antioxidants | Flavonoids and phenolic acids in gel — interest in skin protection (in vitro / traditional context). |
| Minerals and vitamins | Traces of zinc, magnesium, vitamins A, C, E — marginal nutritional contribution vs topical gel use. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Topical hydration | Purified gel for minor burns, dry skin and home cosmetics — lab’s safer baseline. |
| After-sun and skin irritation | Popular cooling relief tradition; mixed evidence — does not replace treatment of severe burns. |
| Internal use (latex / juice) | Historically laxative — today requires strict separation and professional guidance; self-medication discouraged. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Latex and anthraquinones irritate mucous membranes; pregnant, nursing and kidney/liver disease patients should avoid ingestion without supervision. Commercial products should state if anthraquinones were removed.

| Campo | Valor |
|-------|-------|

| Familia | Asphodelaceae |
| Slug del catálogo | `babosa` |
| Fecha de inspección | 2026-07-31 |

## Resumen

Suculenta (*Aloe vera*) muy cultivada; gel foliar rico en polisacáridos — tradición tópica; látex con antraquinonas (aloína) exige precaución si se ingiere.

## Partes usadas

- Hojas (gel)

## Usos tradicionales (catálogo)

- Gel tópico en piel irritada y quemaduras leves (tradición popular)
- Cosmética casera (mascarillas, hidratación)
- Uso interno solo con orientación — distinto del gel externo

## Cuidados

Separar el gel interno de la hoja del látex amarillo (aloína / antraquinonas). Uso interno y extractos concentrados requieren orientación profesional; el látex puede irritar. Contenido educativo — no sustituye una consulta.


## Identidad y etimología

**Babosa** (portugués) describe la consistencia viscosa del gel; **Aloe vera** viene del latín *aloe* (planta amarga) y *vera* (verdadera). No confundir con otras especies de *Aloe*.

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Polisacáridos (acemana) | Gel interno de la hoja — mucílagos hidratantes; marcador citado en estudios del gel depurado. |
| Antraquinonas (aloina / barbaloina) | Concentradas sobre todo en el látex amarillo periférico — efecto laxante; separar gel del látex en preparaciones caseras. |
| Antioxidantes fenólicos | Flavonoides y ácidos fenólicos en el gel — interés en protección cutánea (contexto in vitro / tradicional). |
| Minerales y vitaminas | Trazas de zinc, magnesio, vitaminas A, C, E — aporte nutricional marginal frente al gel tópico. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

## Usos y beneficios (contexto educativo)

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |
| --- | --- |
| Hidratación tópica | Gel depurado en quemaduras leves, piel seca y cosmética casera — línea base más segura del laboratorio. |
| Post-sol e irritación cutánea | Tradición popular de alivio refrescante; evidencia mixta — no sustituye tratamiento de quemaduras graves. |
| Uso interno (látex / jugo) | Históricamente laxante — hoy exige separación rigurosa y orientación profesional; automedicación desaconsejada. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

El látex y las antraquinonas irritan mucosas; embarazadas, lactantes y personas con enfermedad renal/hepática deben evitar la ingestión sin supervisión.

## Scope

Educational inspection of **Chamomile** (*Matricaria chamomilla*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Chamomile** |
| Scientific name | *Matricaria chamomilla* |
| Family | Asteraceae |
| Catalog slug | `camomila` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

Flower heads of *Matricaria chamomilla* — calming tea tradition; markers such as apigenin and blue oil (chamazulene) in educational context.

## Parts used

- Flower heads

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Calming infusions and mild sleep support
- Mild digestive comfort after meals
- Traditional compresses / topical use on irritated skin

## Cautions

Asteraceae allergy possible. Avoid self-medication in pregnancy and young children without guidance. Concentrated essential oils ≠ tea. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Identity and etymology

**Chamomile** from Greek *chamaimēlon* — «ground apple», for the fruity flower scent. Genus **Matricaria** historically linked to the womb in European references.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Apigenin (flavonoid) | Main marker in floral heads — interest in GABAergic modulation and calming effect (in vitro / mild clinical studies). |
| Chamazulene | Formed during essential oil distillation — blue pigment; mild anti-inflammatory in experimental models. |
| α-bisabolol | Sesquiterpene in the oil — skin calming and anti-irritant in topical preparations. |
| Coumarins and flavonoids | Broad phenolic profile in dried heads — contributes to characteristic bitter-sweet taste. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Calming tea and sleep | Mild infusion before sleep — European tradition adapted to Brazil; moderate dose (1–2 cups). |
| Mild digestive comfort | After heavy meals — documented mild antispasodic effect for oil and extracts. |
| Compresses and baths | Topical use for mild skin irritation and tired eyes (folk tradition, not ophthalmological). |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Possible cross-allergy with Asteraceae (daisy, ragweed). Theoretical interactions with anticoagulants at high extract doses — occasional tea differs from supplements.

## Resumen

Capítulos de *Matricaria chamomilla* — tradición de infusiones calmantes; marcadores como apigenina y aceite azul (camazuleno) en contexto educativo.

## Partes usadas

- Capítulos florales

## Usos tradicionales (catálogo)

- Infusiones calmantes y apoyo leve al sueño
- Confort digestivo leve tras comidas
- Compresas / uso tópico tradicional en piel irritada

Posible alergia a Asteraceae. Evitar automedicación en embarazo y niños pequeños sin orientación. Aceites esenciales concentrados ≠ infusión. Contenido educativo — no sustituye una consulta.


## Identidad y etimología

**Manzanilla** / **camomila** del griego *chamaimēlon* — «manzana del suelo». El género **Matricaria** alude históricamente al útero.

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Apigenina (flavonoide) | Marcador principal de los capítulos — interés en modulación GABAérgica y efecto calmante. |
| Camazuleno | Formado en la destilación del aceite esencial — pigmento azul; antiinflamatorio leve en modelos experimentales. |
| α-bisabolol | Sesquiterpeno del aceite — calmante cutáneo y anti-irritante en preparaciones tópicas. |
| Cumarinas y flavonoides | Perfil fenólico amplio en capítulos secos — contribuye al sabor amargo-dulce característico. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |

| Infusión calmante y sueño | Infusión leve antes de dormir — tradición europea adaptada; dosis moderada (1–2 tazas). |
| Conforto digestivo leve | Tras comidas pesadas — efecto antiespasmódico suave documentado para aceite y extractos. |
| Compresas y baños | Uso tópico en irritaciones cutáneas leves (tradición popular). |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

Posible alergia cruzada con Asteraceae. Interacciones teóricas con anticoagulantes en dosis altas de extracto.

## Summary

Citrus grass (*Cymbopogon citratus*) common in home gardens; citral and essential oil in leaves — teas and cooking.

## Parts used

- Leaves

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Aromatic citrus teas
- Flavoring foods and broths
- Mild popular digestive use

## Cautions

Concentrated essential oil is irritating — do not ingest neat. Pregnancy and epilepsy: professional guidance. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Citral (geranial + neral) | Main terpenoid aldehyde (≈65–85% of oil) — lemon aroma; species identity marker. |
| Myrcene and geraniol | Secondary monoterpenes in essential oil — modulate aroma profile and mild relaxing effects. |
| Flavonoids and chlorogenic acid | Present in aqueous infusion — antioxidant contribution beyond volatile oil. |
| Fiber and minerals | Infusion and cooked leaf provide traces of iron, magnesium and insoluble fiber. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Digestive tea and mild febrifuge | Decoction or infusion after meals — Brazilian and Asian folk tradition. |
| Aromatic cuisine | Base for curries, soups and fish — everyday dietary exposure (culinary dose). |
| Insect repellent (topical) | Diluted essential oil — traditional use; patch-test before wide application. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Concentrated essential oil irritates skin and mucous membranes. Caution in pregnancy with undiluted oil. Moderate infusion is the lab’s prudent line.

## Summary

Native shrub (*Baccharis trimera*) — bitter teas of southern/southeastern Brazil; flavonoids and diterpenes in popular digestive tradition.

## Parts used

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Traditional bitter digestive teas
- Popular hepatic/digestive herbal use (cultural context)

## Cautions

Intense bitterness; prolonged use and pregnancy need guidance. Does not replace assessment of liver disease. Educational content — avoid self-medication.


## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Flavonoids (e.g. quercetin, rutin) | Dominant phenolic markers in aerial parts — antioxidant and hepatoprotective interest (animal models). |
| Chlorogenic acid and derivatives | Abundant phenolic acid — common in native bitter plants. |
| Diterpenes and triterpenes | Lipophilic profile in ethanolic extracts — contributes to bitterness and documented bioactivity. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

Hepatotoxicity reported with excessive or non-standardized use. Avoid in pregnancy, nursing and liver disease without supervision. Do not combine with other hepatotoxins. Distinguish from [field rosemary](/plantas/alecrim-do-campo/) (*B. dracunculifolia*), source of green propolis.

## Summary

Equisetum — silica and folk diuretic tradition; aerial parts in teas and baths (do not confuse with toxic species).

## Parts used

- Aerial parts

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Traditional infusions (folk diuresis)
- Baths and topical use
- Interest in silica / connective tissue in tradition

## Cautions

May interact with diuretics and affect kidneys/electrolytes — seek professional guidance. Identify species; some Equisetum are toxic. Educational content.


## Identity and etymology

**Cavalinha** (Portuguese) evokes the segmented stem shape. **Equisetum** from Latin *equus* (horse) + *seta* (bristle) — horsetail.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Silica (silicic acid) | 5–10% silica in dry plant — distinctive marker; deposits in stomata and cell walls. |
| Flavonoids (e.g. quercetin, kaempferol) | Antioxidant contribution of infusion — complements mineral profile. |
| Trace alkaloids (palustrine) | Present in very low concentration — toxicological relevance mainly in concentrated extracts or prolonged use. |
| Minerals (K, Ca, Mg) | Mineral ash profile — basis of «remineralizing» folk tradition. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Diuretic and remineralizing tea | European and Brazilian tradition — short intermittent doses; not a substitute for drinking water. |
| Nails and hair (topical/oral) | Popular metaphor of strengthening via silica — limited clinical evidence. |
| Sitz baths | Topical use for mild inflammation — historical home practice. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Contains thiaminase — may reduce vitamin B1 with chronic use; prefer occasional decoction. Contraindicated in pregnancy and kidney disease. Theoretical interaction with diuretics and lithium.

## Summary

*Mikania glomerata* — classic vine in respiratory syrups and teas; coumarins (e.g. coumarin) in educational context.

## Parts used

- Leaves

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Syrups and teas of popular respiratory medicine
- Traditional expectorant infusions
- Family use for colds (tradition — not a protocol)

## Cautions

Coumarins: caution with anticoagulants and hepatotoxicity at high doses. Do not use in pregnancy without guidance. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Identity and etymology

**Guaco** is of Tupi-Guarani origin (*guaco*, «snake healer») — oral tradition on bites and respiratory use. **Mikania** honors botanist J. Mikan.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Coumarin | 0.5–1% in leaves — characteristic sweet aroma; mild bronchodilator in animal models (do not extrapolate human dose). |
| Lupeol and triterpenes | Pentacyclic triterpenes — mild anti-inflammatory and immunomodulation (in vitro studies). |
| Flavonoids (e.g. kaempferol) | Complement antioxidant profile of fresh or dried leaf. |
| Trace essential oils | Minor monoterpenes — secondary aroma contribution vs coumarin. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| «Expectorant» syrup and tea | Folk medicine for cough and mild bronchitis — coumarin as identity marker of home syrup. |
| Mild bronchodilation (interest) | Animal studies — **not** equivalent to prescribed pharmacological bronchodilator. |
| Popular antipyretic | Tea for colds — tradition combined with honey and lemon (home context). |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Excess coumarin is hepatotoxic (reference also in tonka and cassia). Avoid chronic high doses. Contraindicated in pregnancy, nursing and anticoagulated patients (warfarin).

## Summary

*Mentha spicata* (and allies) — menthol/mint oils in teas and cooking; species and chemotype matter.

## Parts used

- Leaves

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Digestive and refreshing teas
- Cooking and flavoring
- Popular use for mild nausea

## Cautions

Do not confuse species (*M. piperita* vs *spicata*). Concentrated essential oil may irritate; caution in reflux and infants. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Identity and etymology

**Mint** from Latin *hortus* (garden). **Mentha** refers to nymph Mintho in Greek myth; **menthol** derives from the genus.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Carvone (spearmint) | Main terpene in *M. spicata* oil — sweet aroma, distinct from peppermint (menthol). |
| Menthol and menthone (traces) | Present in lower amount than *M. piperita* — confusing species changes profile. |
| Flavonoids (e.g. hesperidin) | Aqueous infusion — antioxidant contribution beyond volatiles. |
| Tannins and phenolic acids | Mild bitterness in prolonged decoctions — moderates «refreshing» effect. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Digestive tea and mild anti-nausea | Fresh or dried leaves — universal tradition for mild dyspepsia and pregnancy (with guidance). |
| Cuisine and beverages | Sauces, iced teas, mocktails — safe dietary exposure at culinary doses. |
| Mild aromatherapy | Inhalation of infusion vapors — sensory comfort; does not replace asthma treatment. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Concentrated essential oil can burn and trigger bronchospasm in asthmatics. *M. piperita* has more menthol — identify species. Caution with reflux (may relax esophageal sphincter).

## Scope

Educational inspection of **False boldo** (*Plectranthus barbatus*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

| Field | Value |

| Family | Lamiaceae |
| Catalog slug | `boldo` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

In Brazil, “boldo” usually means *Plectranthus barbatus* (false boldo) — distinct from Chilean *Peumus boldus*; bitter leaves in digestive teas.

## Parts used

- Leaves

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Traditional bitter digestive teas
- Popular use after heavy meals
- Home herbal use (identify species)

## Cautions

Do not confuse with *Peumus boldus* (Chilean boldo — documented hepatotoxicity in abuse). Prolonged use, pregnancy and liver disease: professional guidance. Educational content.


## Identity and etymology

In Brazil **boldo** mainly means *Plectranthus barbatus* (**false boldo**), though the name is borrowed from Chilean **boldo** (*Peumus boldus* Molina, Monimiaceae) — a distinct species native to Chile, rich in **boldine** with a different hepato-biliary profile.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Diterpenes (e.g. barbatusol) | Markers of *P. barbatus* — **not** boldine from Chilean boldo; confusing species invalidates comparisons. |
| Essential oil (cineole, α-pinene) | Aroma profile distinct from *Peumus* — identifies Brazilian false boldo. |
| Flavonoids and phenolics | Antioxidant activity documented in dried leaves — complements diterpenes. |
| Boldine (absent or trace) | Characteristic alkaloid of *Peumus boldus* — **do not** use as marker for Brazilian false boldo. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Bitter digestive tea | Brazilian home tradition — 1 occasional cup; **not** equivalent to pharmacological Chilean boldo. |
| Hepatic comfort (popular metaphor) | Associated with «cleansing» — weak clinical evidence for *P. barbatus* vs *Peumus* tradition. |
| Ornamental and home medicinal cultivation | Easy to grow — chemical standardization varies; prefer identified dried leaf. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

**Species confusion is a real risk:** *Peumus boldus* has its own contraindications and interactions (biliary obstruction). *P. barbatus* also requires moderation — avoid chronic use, pregnancy and nursing without guidance.

En Brasil, «boldo» suele ser *Plectranthus barbatus* (falso boldo) — distinto del *Peumus boldus* chileno; hojas amargas en infusiones digestivas.

## Identidad y etimología

En Brasil **boldo** designa sobre todo *Plectranthus barbatus* (**falso-boldo**), aunque el nombre se toma del **boldo chileno** (*Peumus boldus*) — especie distinta, nativa de Chile, rica en **boldina**.

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Diterpenos (p. ej. barbatusol) | Marcadores de *P. barbatus* — **no** es boldina del boldo chileno; confundir especies invalida comparaciones. |
| Aceite esencial (cineol, α-pineno) | Perfil aromático distinto de *Peumus* — identifica el falso-boldo brasileño. |
| Flavonoides y fenólicos | Actividad antioxidante documentada en hojas secas — complementa diterpenos. |
| Boldina (ausente o traza) | Alcaloide característico de *Peumus boldus* — **no** usar como marcador del falso-boldo brasileño. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

| --- | --- |
| Infusión digestiva amarga | Tradición doméstica brasileña — 1 taza ocasional; **no** equivalente al boldo chileno farmacológico. |
| Conforto hepático (metáfora popular) | Asociado a «depurar» — evidencia clínica débil para *P. barbatus* vs tradición de *Peumus*. |
| Cultivo ornamental y medicinal doméstico | Planta de fácil cultivo — estandarización química varía; preferir hoja seca identificada. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

**Confusión de especies es riesgo real:** *Peumus boldus* tiene contraindicaciones propias. *P. barbatus* también exige moderación — evitar uso crónico y embarazo sin orientación.

## Summary

*Melissa officinalis* — European lemon balm adapted locally; citral and phenolic acids in calming teas.

## Parts used

- Leaves

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Relaxing infusions
- Flavoring and light cooking
- European tradition of mild nervous comfort

## Cautions

May potentiate sedatives. Hypothyroidism and pregnancy: guidance. Concentrated essential oil ≠ tea. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Identity and etymology

**Melissa** from Greek *mélissa* (μέλισσα) — «bee», for bees’ affinity to the flowers. **Officinalis** indicates historical pharmacy use.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Citral and citronellal | Essential oil — lemon aroma; mild sedation and in vitro antiviral activity (extracts, not pure oral oil). |
| Rosmarinic acid | Abundant phenolic — documented anti-inflammatory and antioxidant; also in rosemary and mint. |
| Flavonoids (e.g. luteolin) | Complement calming effect of aqueous infusion. |
| Tannins | Mild astringency — relevant in long decoctions. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Calming tea and sleep | Evening infusion — European tradition; mild studies on anxiety and subclinical insomnia. |
| Cold sores (topical extract) | Standardized topical extract — moderate evidence; home tea **does not** equal registered cream. |
| Mild digestive | After meals — mild antispasmodic in experimental models. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

May potentiate sedatives and thyroid hormone (in vitro — caution with hypothyroidism). Concentrated oral essential oil is toxic. Distinguish *Melissa* vs *Lippia alba* (Brazilian erva-cidreira).

## Summary

*Salvia rosmarinus* — kitchen shrub; cineole, camphor and phenolic acids in teas and seasoning.

## Parts used

- Leaves
- Sprigs

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Cooking (meats, roasts, oils)
- Aromatic teas
- Popular cognitive-stimulation tradition (cultural context)

## Cautions

Essential oil rich in camphor — do not ingest neat; caution in epilepsy and pregnancy. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Identity and etymology

**Rosemary** from Latin *ros marinus* — «dew of the sea». Reclassified from *Rosmarinus* to *Salvia* (2017).

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Carnosic acid and carnosol | Phenolic diterpenes — potent lipophilic antioxidants; standardized extract markers. |
| Rosmarinic acid | Hydrophilic phenolic — common in fresh leaves and short infusions. |
| 1,8-cineole (eucalyptol) | Monoterpene in essential oil — camphoraceous aroma; mild circulatory stimulant (topical/inhaled). |
| Flavonoids and minor terpenes | Full profile varies with climate and watering — home garden vs wildcrafting. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Aromatic cuisine | Meats, potatoes, breads — classic Mediterranean dietary exposure adapted to Brazil. |
| Mild stimulating tea | Mornings — tradition to «clear the mind»; mild stimulants (does not replace coffee at equivalent dose). |
| Antioxidant preservation | Leaf in oil or salt — traditional preservation (carnosic delays lipid oxidation). |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

High-dose oral essential oil may cause seizures. Contraindicated in pregnancy (traditional emmenagogue). Theoretical interactions with anticoagulants and antihypertensives in concentrated extracts. **Do not confuse** with [field rosemary](/plantas/alecrim-do-campo/) (*Baccharis dracunculifolia*).

## Summary

Rhizome of *Zingiber officinale* — gingerols and shogaols; teas, cooking and anti-nausea tradition (educational context).

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Digestive teas and decoctions
- Cooking (fresh, dried, preserved)

## Cautions

May interact with anticoagulants and irritate the stomach at high doses; caution with gallstones. Culinary use ≠ concentrated extracts. Educational content — does not replace a consultation.


## Identity and etymology

**Ginger** from Latin *zingiber*, borrowed from Sanskrit *śṛṅgavera* (horn shape). Same family (Zingiberaceae) as [turmeric](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-curcuma.html).

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Gingerols (e.g. 6-gingerol) | Pungent phenolics in fresh rhizome — anti-nausea and mild anti-inflammatory (moderate clinical studies). |
| Shogaols (dried/cooked rhizome) | Gingerol degradation products with heat — greater pungency and antioxidant activity when dried. |
| Zingerone and volatile terpenes | Sweet aroma after cooking — sensory marker distinct from fresh. |
| Fiber and minerals | Magnesium, potassium and insoluble fiber — nutritional contribution of powdered or grated fresh rhizome. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Anti-nausea (pregnancy, motion sickness) | Rhizome in tea or standardized capsule — moderate evidence; low dose and prenatal guidance. |
| Culinary digestive and anti-inflammatory | Asian cuisines and teas — everyday dietary exposure as safe line. |
| Mild post-exercise muscle pain | Standardized extracts — mild studies; spicy food ≠ supplement. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

May potentiate anticoagulants and lower blood sugar (monitor diabetics). Gallstones and active ulcer — caution. Interaction with antihypertensives at high doses.

| Scientific name | *Curcuma longa* |
| Family | Zingiberaceae |

## Summary

Yellow rhizome known in Brazil as açafrão-da-terra (Indian saffron) — cooking, teas and popular tradition linked to digestive comfort and anti-inflammatory use (educational context).

## Parts used

- Rhizome

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Cooking (spice and natural colorant)
- Teas and golden milk
- Popular digestive and traditional anti-inflammatory use
- Traditional topical preparations in some cultures

## Cautions

Educational content — does not replace professional advice. Everyday culinary use differs from concentrated curcumin supplements. May interact with anticoagulants and irritate the stomach at high doses; caution with gallstones and in pregnancy. Do not confuse with true saffron (Crocus sativus).


## Identity and etymology

**Turmeric** / **açafrão-da-terra** from Arabic *kurkum* and Persian, referring to the yellow dye — **not** true saffron (*Crocus sativus*). Same family as [ginger](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-gengibre.html) (Zingiberaceae).

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Curcumin (curcuminoids) | 2–5% in dry rhizome — yellow marker; low oral bioavailability without piperine or lipids. |
| Demethoxycurcumin and bisdemethoxycurcumin | Minor curcuminoids — modulate total antioxidant activity of extract. |
| Essential oil (turmerone, atlantone) | Rhizome terpenes — earthy aroma; synergy with curcuminoids in whole extracts. |
| Polysaccharides and fiber | Non-dye fraction of powder — relevant in whole culinary use vs isolated capsule. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Spice and culinary dye | Rice, broths, curry — everyday dietary exposure; lab’s most prudent baseline. |
| Digestive comfort and golden milk | Teas and golden milk — adapted Ayurvedic tradition; combine with fat/pepper for absorption. |
| Anti-inflammatory interest (supplements) | Standardized extracts studied in mild arthritis — **not** equivalent to a spoonful in food. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

May interact with anticoagulants and irritate gallbladder. Concentrated supplements ≠ culinary use. Do not confuse with *Crocus sativus* (true saffron). Caution in pregnancy at high doses.

## Summary

*Carapichea ipecacuanha* — historic root with emetine/cephaeline; pharmacopeia and restricted use (not a home remedy).

- Education on isoquinoline alkaloids

## Cautions

Emetine is toxic in abuse — do not self-medicate or use as a «homemade syrup». Educational content only.


## Identity and etymology

**Ipecacuanha** from Tupi *ipegaa-guene* («dry stem that provokes vomiting») — documented indigenous name.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Emetine (isoquinoline alkaloid) | Main root marker — potent emetic; historical antiprotozoal (amebiasis). |
| Cephaeline | Congener alkaloid — more emetic and less amebicidal than emetine. |
| Secondary alkaloids (e.g. psychotrine) | Full root profile — cumulative toxicity with repeated doses. |
| Triterpenes and amides | Non-alkaloid fraction — lesser historical clinical relevance. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Emergency emetic (historical) | Ipecac syrup — **obsolete** in most modern poisoning protocols; prefer charcoal and emergency services. |
| Amebicide (historical) | Injectable emetine replaced by safer antiparasitics — museum/educational value. |
| Brazilian pharmacognosy reference | Atlantic Forest native — historical chapter of Western pharmacopeia. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

**Toxic — do not use without supervision.** Emetine cardiotoxic with repeated doses. Home root syrup is unpredictable and dangerous.

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

| Fecha de inspección | 2026-07-31 |

## Resumen

*Cinchona* — corteza histórica de la quinina; antimalárico clásico — referencia de farmacopea, no infusión doméstica.

## Partes usadas

- Corteza

## Usos tradicionales (catálogo)

- Referencia histórica antimalárica (quinina)
- Educación sobre alcaloides de la corteza
- Contexto de farmacopea e historia de la medicina

## Cuidados

Quinina y derivados son fármacos potentes — especies y usos regulados; no automedicar con «té de quina». Contenido educativo.


## Identidad y etimología

**Quina** del quechua *kina*. **Quinina** nombra el alcaloide antimalárico histórico.

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Quinina (alcaloide) | Principal alcaloide — amargo intenso; base antimalárica histórica. |
| Quinidina y cinchonina | Alcaloides congéneres — quinidina como antiarrítmico. |
| Cinchonidina y cinchonina | Perfil alcaloide varía por especie. |
| Taninos y flavonoides | Fracción no alcaloide — irrelevante para actividad antimalárica. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Summary

*Cannabis sativa* — cannabinoids (THC, CBD and others) in clinical and training context; UNIFESP focus and law — does not encourage illicit cultivation.

## Parts used

- Flowers
- Extracts (clinical context)

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Education on therapeutic use (UNIFESP course)
- Reference in herbal medicine and Brazilian legislation

## Cautions

Medicinal use is subject to legislation and prescription. In adolescents, longitudinal neuroimaging studies (e.g. IMAGEN / Albaugh et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2021) associate cannabis use with changes in cortical neurodevelopment — see the BudGanja inspection of that article. Educational content — it does not encourage illegal cultivation or self-medication.


## Identity and etymology

**Cannabis** likely from Greek *kánnabis*, possibly Scythian/Persian origin — ancient name for fiber and psychoactive plant. **Sativa** = cultivated.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Δ9-THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) | Main psychoactive — CB1/CB2 agonist; analgesic, antiemetic and psychoactive dose-dependent effects. |
| CBD (cannabidiol) | Non-classically psychoactive — modulates THC; interest in refractory epilepsy and anxiety (registered products). |
| Terpenes (myrcene, limonene, pinene) | Volatile profile — discussed «entourage effect»; modulates aroma and possibly effects. |
| Acid cannabinoids (THCA, CBDA) | Forms in fresh plant — convert with heat/decarboxylation. |
| Cannabinoid flavonoids (cannflavins) | Exclusive phenolic compounds — in vitro anti-inflammatory (research). |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Regulated medicinal use | Prescription and registered products — **not** equivalent to recreational use or self-medication with unanalyzed material. |
| Chronic pain, spasticity, oncology nausea | Indications with variable evidence — individualized clinical decision; prefer standardized formulations. |
| UNIFESP education and Brazilian legislation | Lab training context — separate science, policy and legal clinical access. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

**Medicinal use subject to legislation and prescription.** In adolescents, longitudinal studies (e.g. Albaugh et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2021) link cannabis to cortical neurodevelopment changes. Does not encourage illicit cultivation.

inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.contentEn:
## Scope

Editorial inspection of **sugarcane** (*Saccharum officinarum* L.) — botanical origin vs **refined sugar** / free sugars. Crosses [Dr. Lair Ribeiro](/posts/post-inspecao-divulgacao-lair-ribeiro.html) outreach on sugar/fructose/diabesity after a full channel title scan (887 videos).

> **Method note:** WHO free-sugars guidance + Lair portal/channel audit. **Not medical advice.** Indexing ≠ endorsement. The plant is not the villain.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Sugarcane** |
| Scientific name | *Saccharum officinarum* L. |
| Family | Poaceae |
| BudGanja type | Risk derivative — plant → industrial product |
| Risk product in focus | Refined sugar / free sugars in ultra-processed foods |
| Inspection date | 2026-08-01 |

## Botanical origin

Sugarcane is a tropical perennial grass grown for sucrose-rich stems. Domestication traces to **New Guinea / Southeast Asia**, then India and the medieval Islamic world, Europe, and — with colonial expansion — the Americas.

In **Brazil**, cane became an economic axis from the 16th century (mills, slavery, the sugar cycle). Juice, molasses and artisanal uses are part of food culture; the modern problem is not the plant’s existence, but the scale of **refining** and the ubiquity of **free sugars** in drinks and ultra-processed foods.

## From plant to risk product

| Stage | What happens | Editorial risk |
|-------|--------------|----------------|
| Plant | Stem harvest; natural sucrose in juice | Low — food/culture, traditional context |
| Processing | Milling, clarification, crystallization | Intermediate — concentrates sugar |
| Industrial refining | High-purity white/crystal sugar | High when daily intake explodes |
| Ultra-processed foods | Soft drinks, snacks, industrial sweets | High — free sugars + calorie density |

## What public health highlights

WHO guidance limits **free sugars** — typically under **10%** of daily energy, with additional benefit below **5%** for some outcomes (e.g. dental caries). High intake is linked to dental caries, excess energy/weight gain, and poor diet quality when ultra-processed foods displace real food.

Sources: [WHO — sugars and dental caries](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/sugars-and-dental-caries) · [WHO sugars guideline (2015)](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241549028).

## Cross-link — Dr. Lair Ribeiro

Channel scan: 887 titles; hits in [`lair-sugar-hits.json`](/content/channels/lair-sugar-hits.json). Portal [Part 4 — carbohydrates](https://lairribeiro.com.br/parte-4-inflamacoes-cronica-causada-por-carboidratos/) names **sugarcane** (or beet) as the source of table **sucrose** and frames excess sugar/fructose as metabolic risk. Anchor videos: Truths about Sugar (`UfPawBg7vXc`), Fructose the unknown poison (`rVS2M4wuseE`), Sugar and Sweeteners (`oGhMcYmy-C4`). Full sheet: [Lair](/posts/post-inspecao-divulgacao-lair-ribeiro.html).

## Origen botánico

La caña es una gramínea tropical perenne. La domesticación remonta a **Nueva Guinea / Sudeste Asiático**; llegó a las Américas con la expansión colonial. En **Brasil**, fue eje económico desde el siglo XVI. El problema moderno no es la planta, sino la escala de **refinación** y los **azúcares libres** en ultraprocesados.

## De la planta al producto de riesgo

| Etapa | Qué ocurre | Riesgo editorial |
|-------|------------|------------------|
| Planta | Cosecha del tallo; sacarosa natural | Bajo — comida/cultura |
| Procesamiento | Molienda y cristalización | Intermedio |
| Refinación industrial | Azúcar de alta pureza | Alto si la dosis diaria explota |
| Ultraprocesados | Refrescos, snacks, dulces | Alto |

## Salud pública

La OMS recomienda limitar los **azúcares libres** (p. ej. menos del **10%** de la energía diaria). El exceso se asocia a caries, exceso energético y dietas pobres cuando el ultraprocesado sustituye comida real.

inspecao-planta-abacate.contentEn:
## Scope

Educational inspection of **Avocado** (*Persea americana Mill.*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/plantas/abacate/](/plantas/abacate/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Avocado** |
| Scientific name | *Persea americana Mill.* |
| Family | Lauraceae |
| Catalog slug | `abacate` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

Mesoamerican fruit (*āhuacatl* in Nahuatl): pulp rich in monounsaturated fats; everyday food in Brazil — this sheet separates the whole plant from sugary, additive-laden industrial derivatives.

## Parts used

- Fruit (pulp)
- Pulp oil (culinary / traditional cosmetic)
- Leaves (traditional use, with caution — not for pets)

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Food and cooking (salads, fresh guacamole, toast)
- Mesoamerican and Andean food ethnobotany (aguacate / palta)
- Home pulp preparations (skin/hair — popular tradition)
- Pressed oil in artisanal contexts

## Cautions

Ripe pulp is common food. Leaves, peel and seed contain persin and may be toxic to animals (dogs, birds, etc.). Leaf extracts/teas: avoid self-medication. Industrial derivatives with sugar and additives have their own Risk derivatives sheet. Educational content — does not replace professional advice.


## Identity and etymology

The Portuguese **abacate** comes from Nahuatl **āhuacatl** (via Spanish *aguacate*) — language of Mesoamerican indigenous peoples. In Nahuatl the same word names the **fruit** and also **testicle**, by shape; fertility/vigor cultural charge in ethnobotany. **Not** a Tupi word. In the Andes often called **palta**.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Monounsaturated lipids (MUFA) | Predominantly **monounsaturated** fats (oleic acid); also palmitic and linoleic — dietary cardioprotective profile. |
| Persin | Lipid antifungal toxin — concentrated in leaves, seed and skin; toxic to many pets. |
| Polyphenol oxidase (PPO) | Enzyme that browns cut pulp — oxidative browning (does not indicate immediate spoilage). |
| Carotenoids and vitamin E | Lutein, α-tocopherol — lipophilic antioxidants in ripe pulp. |
| Fiber and potassium | Low free sugar vs many fruits; fiber and potassium relevant in food matrix. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Whole food (ripe pulp) | Salads, fresh guacamole, toast — lab low-risk line; intact food matrix. |
| Cardio-healthy lipid profile | Replacing saturated fats with MUFA — nutritional context, not «superfood» claim. |
| Mesoamerican ethnobotany | Ancient fruit (*āhuacatl* / *palta*) — cultural and food credit independent of industrial marketing. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Ripe pulp is common food. Leaves, skin and seed contain persin — **do not** feed to pets. Leaf extracts: avoid self-medication. Industrial derivatives with sugar and additives have separate Risk Derivatives sheet.

- [Inspection: Avocado derivatives — sugar, additives and industrial chemistry](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-abacate.html)

Inspección educativa de **Aguacate** (*Persea americana Mill.*) del catálogo de plantas medicinales del Inspetor BudGanja. Este informe reúne la ficha pública con método verificable del laboratorio — **no** es un protocolo clínico y **no sustituye** orientación profesional de salud.

## Resumen

Fruto mesoamericano (*āhuacatl* en náhuatl): pulpa rica en grasas monoinsaturadas; alimento corriente en Brasil — la ficha separa la planta entera de los derivados industriales azucarados y aditivados.

## Partes usadas

- Fruto (pulpa)
- Aceite de la pulpa (culinario / cosmético tradicional)
- Hojas (uso tradicional, con cautela — no alimentar animales)

## Usos tradicionales (catálogo)

- Alimento y cocina (ensaladas, guacamole fresco, tostadas)
- Etnobotánica alimentaria mesoamericana y andina (aguacate / palta)
- Preparaciones caseras con la pulpa (piel/cabello — tradición popular)
- Aceite prensado en contextos artesanales

## Cuidados

La pulpa madura es alimento común. Hojas, cáscara y hueso contienen persina y pueden ser tóxicos para animales (perros, aves, etc.). Extractos y té de hoja: evitar automedicación. Los derivados industriales con azúcar y aditivos tienen ficha propia en Derivados de riesgo. Contenido educativo — no sustituye orientación profesional.


## Identidad y etimología

La palabra **abacate** / **aguacate** viene del náhuatl **āhuacatl** — lengua mesoamericana. Nombra el **fruto** y también **testículo** por la forma. **No** es palabra tupí. En los Andes suele llamarse **palta**.

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Lípidos monoinsaturados (MUFA) | Predominan grasas **monoinsaturadas** (ácido oleico); perfil cardioprotector alimentario. |
| Persina | Toxina antifúngica — concentrada en hojas, hueso y cáscara; tóxica para mascotas. |
| Polifenol oxidasa (PPO) | Enzima que oscurece la pulpa cortada — pardeamiento oxidativo. |
| Carotenoides y vitamina E | Luteína, α-tocoferol — antioxidantes lipofílicos en pulpa madura. |
| Fibras y potasio | Bajo azúcar libre vs muchas frutas; fibra y potasio relevantes. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

## Usos y beneficios (contexto educativo)

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |
| --- | --- |
| Alimento integral (pulpa madura) | Ensaladas, guacamole fresco — línea de bajo riesgo; matriz alimentaria intacta. |
| Perfil lipídico cardiosaludable | Sustitución de grasas saturadas por MUFA — contexto nutricional. |
| Etnobotánica mesoamericana | Fruto milenario — crédito cultural independiente de marketing industrial. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

Pulpa madura es alimento común. Hojas y carozo contienen persina — **no** alimentar animales. Derivados industriales tienen ficha propia.
