## Scope

Editorial and **chemical** inspection of **industrial avocado derivatives** (*Persea americana*) — credit the whole fruit, audit oils, shelf guacamole, desserts and drinks where **sugar**, syrups and **chemical additives** reshape the matrix. Cross-links: [Avocado plant sheet](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-abacate.html), [Sugarcane / free sugars](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html).

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit. Starting points: plant catalog, Wikipedia, WHO free sugars / ultra-processed debate, Anvisa additives framing. **Not medical advice.** Not a brand lab test. Plant ≠ villain; focus is **transformed food matrix**.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Origin plant | Avocado — [plant inspection](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-abacate.html) |
| BudGanja type | Risk derivative — fruit → industrial product |
| Focus | Refined oil, industrial guacamole/spreads, sugary avocado drinks/desserts, ultra-processed snacks |
| Chemical focus | Free sugars + additives (preservatives, emulsifiers, acidulants, flavours, thickeners) |
| Date | 2026-08-01 |

## Hypotheses

**H1:** whole ripe pulp ≠ ultra-processed “avocado” marketing matrix.  
**H2:** risk axis = **sugar + energy density + formulation additives + frequency**.  
**H3:** label literacy is the repeatable tool.

## Chemistry map (summary)

| Stage | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| Whole pulp | MUFA (oleic), fibre, K, E; PPO browning; persin in leaves/seed |
| Fresh guacamole | Low process; lemon acid slows PPO |
| Virgin / refined oil | Lipid concentrate; refining removes volatiles |
| Shelf paste / dessert / shake | Often sugar + emulsifiers + preservatives + flavours |

## Additive functions (educational)

Sugar / HFCS / maltodextrin · citric/ascorbic acids · sorbate/benzoate · EDTA (where allowed) · lecithin / E471 · xanthan / modified starches · flavours/colours · salt — see Portuguese sheet for full table. Cross [sugarcane](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html).

## Health framing

WHO free-sugars limits; energy density of oil+sugar matrices; sodium in savoury pastes; don’t eat leaves/seed (persin). **Editorial verdict:** credit the fruit; alert on sugary additive-laden derivatives.

## Status

**Approved in Risk derivatives** — avocado as fruit vs industrial sugar×additives matrix.

inspecao-planta-coco.contentEn:
## Scope

Educational inspection of **Coconut** (*Cocos nucifera L.*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/plantas/coco/](/plantas/coco/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Coconut** |
| Scientific name | *Cocos nucifera L.* |
| Family | Arecaceae |
| Catalog slug | `coco` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

Tropical palm (*Cocos nucifera*): the fruit (drupe) yields water, pulp and oil — this sheet separates whole coconut and fresh water from sweetened, refined and ultra-processed industrial derivatives.

## Parts used

- Fruit (endosperm water)
- Pulp / kernel (fresh or dried)
- Pulp oil (culinary / traditional cosmetic)
- Husk fiber (coir — material use, not food)

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Fresh coconut water (hydration and tropical drink)
- Pulp in coastal and Afro-Brazilian cooking
- Coconut oil and milk in traditional cuisine
- Material use of husk and palm wood

## Cautions

Fresh water and pulp are common foods. Industrial derivatives with sugar, syrups and additives (sweetened coconut water, desserts, snacks) have their own Risk derivatives sheet. Coconut oil is high in saturated fat — dose and dietary context matter. Educational content — does not replace professional advice.


## Identity and etymology

Portuguese **coco** (fruit) ties to the folk word for **bogeyman** (*coco*): Portuguese sailors saw a **face** in the three “eyes” of the shell — hence the fruit name and genus *Cocos*. In Brazilian Portuguese **coco** can also mean **head** (slang) — figurative, not botanical. Scientific name: *Cocos nucifera* L. (Arecaceae).

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Endosperm water | Sterile liquid in young fruit — electrolytes (K, Na, Mg), natural sugars in moderate dose; distinct from sweetened industrial drinks. |
| Pulp lipids (lauric) | Oil rich in **medium-chain saturated fatty acids** (lauric, myristic); profile unlike olive/avocado — dose and dietary context. |
| Fiber and pulp | Fresh or dried pulp (copra) — fiber and energy; sweetened shredded coconut is already an industrial matrix. |
| Coir / husk | Husk fiber — material use (ropes, substrates); **not** food. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh coconut water | Low-process tropical drink — lab credit line; do not confuse with sweetened bottled products. |
| Coastal cooking and coconut milk | Pulp and milk in stews, traditional sweets and Afro-Brazilian cooking — culinary matrix, not «superfood». |
| Artisanal vs refined oil | Artisanal pressing ≠ industrial refined oil — see Derivatives sheet for MCT marketing and ultra-processed products. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Fresh water and pulp are common foods. Coconut oil: high saturation — dose. Industrial derivatives with sugar and additives have a separate Risk Derivatives sheet. Not medical advice.

## Alcance

Inspección educativa de **Coco** (*Cocos nucifera L.*) del catálogo de plantas medicinales del Inspetor BudGanja. Este informe reúne la ficha pública con método verificable del laboratorio — **no** es un protocolo clínico y **no sustituye** orientación profesional de salud.

> **Nota metodológica:** auditoría independiente BudGanja a partir de la ficha en [/plantas/coco/](/plantas/coco/). Solo contenido educativo.

## Objeto inspeccionado

| Campo | Valor |
|-------|-------|
| Nombre popular | **Coco** |
| Nombre científico | *Cocos nucifera L.* |
| Familia | Arecaceae |
| Slug del catálogo | `coco` |
| Fecha de inspección | 2026-07-31 |

## Resumen

Palmera tropical (*Cocos nucifera*): el fruto (drupa) ofrece agua, pulpa y aceite — la ficha separa el coco entero y el agua fresca de los derivados industriales endulzados, refinados y ultraprocesados.

## Partes usadas

- Fruto (agua endospérmica)
- Pulpa / almendra (fresca o deshidratada)
- Aceite de la pulpa (culinario / cosmético tradicional)
- Fibra de la cáscara (coir — uso material, no alimentario)

## Usos tradicionales (catálogo)

- Agua de coco fresca (hidratación y bebida tropical)
- Pulpa en cocina costera y afrobrasileña
- Aceite y leche de coco en cocina tradicional
- Uso material de la cáscara y la madera de la palmera

## Cuidados

El agua y la pulpa frescas son alimentos comunes. Los derivados industriales con azúcar, jarabes y aditivos (agua de coco endulzada, postres, snacks) tienen ficha propia en Derivados de riesgo. El aceite de coco es rico en grasa saturada — importan dosis y contexto. Contenido educativo — no sustituye orientación profesional.


## Identidad y etimología

El portugués **coco** (fruto) se liga a la palabra popular para **coco / fantasma**: los navegantes vieron un **rostro** en los tres «ojos» de la cáscara — de ahí el nombre y el género *Cocos*. En Brasil, **coco** también puede significar **cabeza** (jerga). Nombre científico: *Cocos nucifera* L.

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Agua endospérmica | Líquido estéril en fruto joven — electrolitos; distinto de bebidas industriales endulzadas. |
| Lípidos de la pulpa (láurico) | Aceite rico en **ácidos grasos saturados de cadena media** (láurico); dosis y contexto importan. |
| Fibra y pulpa | Pulpa fresca o deshidratada — fibra y energía; coco rallado azucarado ya es matriz industrial. |
| Coir / cáscara | Fibra de la cáscara — uso material; **no** es alimento. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

## Usos y beneficios (contexto educativo)

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |
| --- | --- |
| Agua de coco fresca | Bebida tropical de bajo procesamiento — no confundir con botella endulzada. |
| Cocina costera y leche de coco | Pulpa y leche en cocina tradicional afrobrasileña — matriz culinaria. |
| Aceite artesanal vs refinado | Prensado artesanal ≠ aceite refinado industrial — ver ficha Derivados. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

Agua y pulpa frescas son alimentos comunes. Aceite de coco: alta saturación — dosis. Derivados industriales tienen ficha propia. No es consejo médico.

## Scope

Educational inspection of **Orange** (*Citrus × sinensis (L.) Osbeck*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/plantas/laranja/](/plantas/laranja/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Orange** |
| Scientific name | *Citrus × sinensis (L.) Osbeck* |
| Family | Rutaceae |
| Catalog slug | `laranja` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

Hybrid citrus (*Citrus × sinensis*): credit whole fruit and fresh juice; this sheet separates concentrates, nectars and “orange” soft drinks with sugar and additives.

## Parts used

- Fruit (pulp / segments)
- Freshly squeezed natural juice (low process)
- Peel / zest in cooking (essential oil — dose)
- Home culinary uses without ultra-processing

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Whole / fresh fruit
- Fresh home-squeezed juice (no concentrate or syrup)
- Home cooking (zest, artisanal preserves without industrial additives)
- Mediterranean and tropical food ethnobotany (Rutaceae / *Citrus*)

## Cautions

Fresh fruit is common food. Even “natural” juice concentrates sugar without pulp fiber — dose matters. Industrial derivatives belong in Risk derivatives. Educational — not professional advice.


## Identity and etymology

Portuguese **laranja** comes from Arabic **nāranj** (via Persian / Sanskrit *nāraṅga*), naming bitter citrus; Spanish **naranja** and English *orange* share the chain. Scientific *Citrus × sinensis* marks Asian origin and **hybrid** status in the *Citrus* complex. Portuguese **laranja** usually means the sweet table fruit — distinct from **sour orange** (*Citrus × aurantium*) used in bitters and fragrance.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) | Classic marker of pulp and fresh juice — sensitive to heat, light and long storage. |
| Flavonoids (hesperidin, naringenin) | Mostly peel and albedo — bitterness and antioxidant interest of the whole matrix. |
| Essential oils (d-limonene) | Peel / zest — characteristic aroma; dose and skin irritation possible in concentrated oils. |
| Organic acids (citric) | Acidity and flavour; profile shifts by cultivar (Pera, Bahia, Valencia, etc.). |
| Fiber and intact matrix | Whole fruit keeps fiber and slower sugar dose vs juice or industrial concentrate. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Whole fruit | Lab credit line — fiber + micronutrients in intact matrix. |
| Fresh juice vs concentrate | Fresh-squeezed ≠ reconstituted carton juice; concentrate + sugar = industrial route. |
| Citrus and N in culture | In the inputs research map, high N in citrus can raise size but unbalance flavour/texture — see organic vs industrial map. |
| “Orange” soft drinks | Marketing name/colour ≠ fruit; free sugar + flavours + colours — cross sugarcane / free sugars. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Fresh fruit is common food. Juice: sugar dose without fiber. Peel and essential oils: irritation and photosensitivity possible when concentrated. Sweetened/aromatised industrial derivatives — Derivatives sheet (queue) and free-sugars cross-link. Not medical advice.

## Resumen

Cítrico híbrido (*Citrus × sinensis*): crédito al fruto entero y jugo fresco; la ficha separa concentrados, néctares y refrescos «de naranja» con azúcar y aditivos.

## Partes usadas

- Etnobotánica alimentaria mediterránea y tropical (Rutaceae / *Citrus*)

## Cuidados

El fruto fresco es alimento común. El jugo, aunque «natural», concentra azúcar sin fibra — importa la dosis. Los derivados industriales entran en Derivados de riesgo. Contenido educativo — no sustituye orientación profesional.


## Identidad y etimología

El portugués **laranja** / español **naranja** vienen del árabe **nāranj** (vía persa / sánscrito *nāraṅga*). El nombre científico *Citrus × sinensis* señala origen asiático y carácter **híbrido**. La **naranja dulce** de mesa se distingue de la **naranja amarga** (*Citrus × aurantium*) de amargos y perfumería.

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Vitamina C (ácido ascórbico) | Marcador clásico de pulpa y jugo fresco — sensible a calor, luz y almacenamiento largo. |
| Flavonoides (hesperidina, naringenina) | Sobre todo cáscara y albedo — amargor e interés antioxidante de la matriz entera. |
| Aceites esenciales (d-limoneno) | Cáscara / zest — aroma característico; dosis e irritación cutánea posibles en aceites concentrados. |
| Ácidos orgánicos (cítrico) | Acidez y sabor; el perfil cambia por cultivar. |
| Fibra y matriz intacta | El fruto entero mantiene fibra y dosis más lenta de azúcar frente al jugo o concentrado industrial. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

## Usos y beneficios (contexto educativo)

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |
| --- | --- |
| Fruto entero | Línea de crédito del laboratorio — fibra + micronutrientes en matriz intacta. |
| Jugo fresco vs concentrado | Exprimido al momento ≠ jugo de caja reconstituido; concentrado + azúcar = ruta industrial. |
| Cítricos y N en cultivo | En el mapa de insumos, N alto puede aumentar tamaño pero desequilibrar sabor/textura. |
| «Naranja» en refrescos | Nombre y color de marketing ≠ fruto; azúcar libre + aromas + colorantes — cruzar caña / azúcares libres. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

Fruto fresco es alimento común. Jugo: dosis de azúcar sin fibra. Cáscara y aceites esenciales: irritación y fotosensibilidad posibles en uso concentrado. Derivados industriales — ficha Derivados (cola) y cruce con azúcares libres. No es consejo médico.

## Scope

## Summary

Common Brazilian fruit: whole guava vs guava paste, pulps and sugar-rich nectars.

## Parts used

- Fruit (pulp / natural juice)
- Low-process culinary uses

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Whole / fresh fruit
- Home cooking without ultra-processing

## Cautions

Fresh fruit is common food. Industrial derivatives with sugar, syrups and additives belong in Risk derivatives. Educational content — not professional advice.


## Identity and etymology

Portuguese **goiaba** (and Spanish *guayaba*) comes via Taíno/Arawakan *guayabo* — a Caribbean language — and spread with the plant across the Americas. In Brazil it is a backyard and table fruit; **Psidium guajava** L. (**Myrtaceae**) names the guava tree. **Do not** invent an exclusive Tupi etymology: the name traveled through colonial contact and European botany.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) | Ripe pulp and peel — high content vs many citrus fruits; educational nutrition interest, not a therapeutic dose. |
| Lycopene (pink cultivars) | Red-pink carotenoid in colored pulp — color marker and lipophilic antioxidant of the fresh matrix. |
| Pectin and fiber | Soluble/insoluble fiber in whole fruit; industrial **guava paste** concentrates pectin + sugar — matrix changes. |
| Polyphenols (ellagic / tannins) | Leaves and peel rich in tannins — folk astringent-tea tradition; the lab mainly inspects the **fresh fruit**. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Whole / fresh fruit | Table consumption, vitamins and fiber in intact matrix — lab credit line. |
| Home cooking (low processing) | Home jams and natural juice without syrup — distinct from slab paste and industrial nectars. |
| Guava paste and sugary derivatives | Paste, sweetened pulp and nectar belong in Risk Derivatives / free-sugars conversation — do not confuse with the fruit. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Fresh fruit is common food. Leaf teas and concentrated extracts: folk tradition ≠ clinical protocol — avoid self-medication. Industrial derivatives with sugar and additives (paste, nectars) have their own Risk Derivatives framing. Educational content — not professional advice.

| Polifenoles (elágico / taninos) | Hojas y cáscara ricas en taninos — tradición de infusión astringente; el laboratorio inspecciona sobre todo el **fruto fresco**. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

## Usos y beneficios (contexto educativo)

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |
| --- | --- |
| Fruto entero / fresco | Consumo en mesa, vitaminas y fibra en matriz intacta — línea de crédito del laboratorio. |
| Cocina casera (bajo procesamiento) | Mermeladas caseras y jugo natural — distinto de pasta industrial y néctares. |
| Pasta de guayaba y derivados azucarados | Pasta, pulpa endulzada y néctar entran en Derivados de riesgo — no confundir con el fruto. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

El fruto fresco es alimento común. Infusiones de hoja y extractos: tradición ≠ protocolo clínico. Derivados industriales tienen encuadre propio. Contenido educativo — no sustituye orientación profesional.

inspecao-derivado-caseina.titleEs: Inspección: Caseína — leche bovina y proteína nociva para el organismo
inspecao-derivado-caseina.excerptEn: Harmful products: milk casein (*Bos taurus*) — A1/BCM-7, inflammation (evidence limits) and ultra-processed dairy versus traditional milk. Links gluten and the cattle sheet.
inspecao-derivado-caseina.excerptEs: Productos nocivos: caseína de la leche (*Bos taurus*) — A1/BCM-7, inflamación (límites) y lácteos ultraprocesados frente a leche tradicional. Vínculo con gluten y ficha de la vaca.
inspecao-derivado-caseina.contentEn:
## Scope

Editorial inspection of **cow's milk** and **casein** — the dominant milk protein — as a **product harmful to the body** when intake pattern, protein genetics and ultra-processed dairy collide. Cross-links the [cattle sheet](/animais/vaca/) and the sibling [gluten](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-gluten.html) inspection.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit. **Not medical or dietary advice.** The animal and traditional fresh milk are not absolute villains; the focus is **industrial casein**, dose and inflammation hypotheses with evidence limits.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Popular name | **Casein** (cow's milk) |
| Animal origin | *Bos taurus* — [cattle sheet](/animais/vaca/) |
| BudGanja type | Harmful product — animal protein → industrial matrix |
| Risk focus | Casein (esp. A1 β-casein) + ultra-processed dairy |
| Series | Harmful products |
| Inspection date | 2026-08-02 |

## What casein is

Casein is about **80%** of cow's milk protein (the rest is mainly whey). In cheese, yogurt, milk powder, supplements and many ultra-processed foods, casein is concentrated, heated, mixed with additives or isolated as an industrial ingredient (sodium/calcium caseinate).

## A1 casein, BCM-7 and inflammation (evidence limits)

β-casein has genetic variants (**A1** / **A2**). A1, common in industrial dairy breeds, may release **BCM-7** during digestion. Outreach and parts of the literature link BCM-7 to low-grade inflammation and gut discomfort that is **not** only lactose intolerance.

**Limits:** human evidence is **heterogeneous**. Lactose intolerance ≠ casein sensitivity. This is **label and origin literacy**, not a clinical protocol.

## Labels to watch

- «milk protein», «sodium/calcium caseinate», «dairy solids»;
- sweetened dairy drinks and high-dose casein bars/shakes;
- marketing that hides ultra-processing.

## Sibling — gluten

Casein and [gluten](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-gluten.html) are dense structural proteins abundant in industrial diets — distinct axes, same **Harmful products** category.

## Hub

Return to [Harmful products](/biblioteca/inspecoes/#inspecoes-derivados) and the [animals catalog](/animais/).
inspecao-derivado-caseina.contentEs:
## Alcance

Inspección editorial de la **leche de vaca** y la **caseína** — proteína dominante de la leche — como **producto nocivo para el organismo** cuando dosis, genética proteica y lácteos ultraprocesados se cruzan. Cruza con la [ficha de la vaca](/animais/vaca/) y la inspección hermana del [gluten](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-gluten.html).

> **Nota metodológica:** auditoría independiente BudGanja. **No es consejo médico ni nutricional.** El animal y la leche fresca tradicional no son villanos absolutos; el foco es la **caseína industrial**, la dosis y las hipótesis de inflamación con límites de evidencia.

## Objeto inspeccionado

| Campo | Valor |
|-------|-------|
| Nombre | **Caseína** (leche bovina) |
| Origen animal | *Bos taurus* — [ficha](/animais/vaca/) |
| Tipo BudGanja | Producto nocivo — proteína animal → matriz industrial |
| Producto de riesgo | Caseína (esp. β-caseína A1) + lácteos ultraprocesados |
| Serie | Productos nocivos |
| Fecha | 2026-08-02 |

## Qué es la caseína

La caseína es cerca del **80%** de las proteínas de la leche de vaca. En queso, yogur, leche en polvo, suplementos y ultraprocesados se concentra o se aísla (caseinato de sodio/calcio).

## Caseína A1, BCM-7 e inflamación (límites)

La β-caseína A1 puede liberar **BCM-7** en la digestión. Hipótesis de divulgación asocian BCM-7 a inflamación de bajo grado y malestar digestivo que **no** es solo intolerancia a la lactosa.

**Límites:** evidencia humana heterogénea. Intolerancia a la lactosa ≠ sensibilidad a la caseína. Esto es **alfabetización de etiqueta**, no protocolo clínico.

## Etiquetas a observar

- «proteína de la leche», «caseinato», «sólidos lácteos»;
- bebidas lácteas azucaradas y barras con caseína aislada;
- marketing que oculta ultraprocesamiento.

## Hermana — gluten

Caseína y [gluten](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-gluten.html) son proteínas estructurales densas de dietas industriales — ejes distintos, misma categoría **Productos nocivos**.

inspecao-derivado-gluten.contentEn:
## Scope

Editorial inspection of **gluten** — the wheat protein complex — as a **harmful product** in celiac disease, sensitivity and ultra-processed **flour** matrices. Cross-links [casein](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-caseina.html), [sugarcane / free sugars](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html), [industrial chocolate](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-chocolate.html), and the cultural book [Wheat Belly](/posts/post-inspecao-arte-barriga-de-trigo.html) / [William Davis](/posts/post-inspecao-figura-william-davis.html).

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit. **Not medical advice.** Wheat as a crop is not an absolute villain; the focus is **gluten in industrial matrices** and real clinical axes. Davis’s book is discourse to audit — it does not replace this product sheet.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Name | **Gluten** |
| Botanical origin | Wheat (*Triticum* spp.); also barley, rye |
| Series | Harmful products |
| Inspection date | 2026-08-02 |

## What gluten is

Gluten (gliadins + glutenins) gives dough elasticity. In traditional bread it is cultural; in ultra-processed foods it becomes an omnipresent industrial protein.

## From grain to risk product

| Stage | Editorial risk |
|-------|----------------|
| Grain / culture | Low |
| Refined flour | Intermediate |
| Ultra-processed | High — gluten + sugars + additives |

## Sibling — casein

See [Casein / milk inspection](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-caseina.html).

inspecao-derivado-chocolate.titleEn: Inspection: Industrial chocolate — cacao, sugar, flour and milk
inspecao-derivado-chocolate.titleEs: Inspección: Chocolate industrial — cacao, azúcar, harina y leche
inspecao-derivado-chocolate.excerptEn: Harmful products: industrial chocolate as a matrix joining cacao, sugar, flour/wheat/gluten, milk/casein, Wheat Belly (Davis) and the catalogued lexicon — the hub that relates everything.
inspecao-derivado-chocolate.excerptEs: Productos nocivos: chocolate industrial como matriz que junta cacao, azúcar, harina/trigo/gluten, leche/caseína, Barriga de Trigo (Davis) y el léxico catalogado — hub que relaciona todo.
inspecao-derivado-chocolate.contentEn:
## Scope

Editorial inspection of **industrial chocolate** as an ultra-processed matrix joining **cacao**, **sugar**, **wheat flour/gluten**, **milk/casein**, and the cultural thesis of [Wheat Belly](/posts/post-inspecao-arte-barriga-de-trigo.html) / [William Davis](/posts/post-inspecao-figura-william-davis.html). Hub under [Harmful products](/biblioteca/inspecoes/#inspecoes-derivados); lexicon via the [Words Guide](/guia/palavras.html).

> **Method note:** independent audit. **Not medical advice.** [Cacao](/plantas/cacau/) as a plant is not the villain; factory chocolate is. Indexing Davis/Lair ≠ endorsing every claim.

## Full relation network

| Link | BudGanja sheet |
|------|----------------|
| Cacao | [Plant](/plantas/cacau/) · [Fruit inspection](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-cacau.html) |
| Sugar | [Sugarcane / free sugars](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html) · [Lair](/posts/post-inspecao-divulgacao-lair-ribeiro.html) |
| Flour / gluten / wheat | [Gluten](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-gluten.html) · [Wheat Belly](/posts/post-inspecao-arte-barriga-de-trigo.html) · [Davis](/posts/post-inspecao-figura-william-davis.html) |
| Milk / casein | [Casein](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-caseina.html) |
| Video archive | [Harms × videos](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-analise-danos-videos.html) |
| Candy-coated format | [End of the line](/posts/post-inspecao-expressao-fim-da-linha.html) — shell = [tape](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-cinta.html), core = [life](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-vida.html) |

## Wheat Belly applies here

Chocolate **cookies/wafers** are often wheat + sugar + fat with cacao perfume — the same modern-wheat axis Davis attacks. BudGanja keeps celiac as the clinical gluten axis and treats Davis as cultural discourse.

## Catalogued words (marketing + method)

| Word | Role on the shelf |
|------|-------------------|
| [Path](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-caminho.html) / [Pass](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-passar.html) | Bean → factory → snack; what “passes” on the label |
| [Drug](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-droga.html) | Comfort → habit narrative (lexical parallel, not pharmacology) |
| [Emotion](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-emocao.html) / [Joy](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-alegria.html) | Packaging sells feeling, not the bean |

pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.titleEn: Research: From molecule to waste — pharmaceuticals, industry and inequality
pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.titleEs: Investigación: De la molécula a la basura — fármacos, industria y desigualdad
pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.excerptEn: Preliminary map: drugs and industrial derivatives in the take–make–waste cycle — waste, excess and harm to plants, animals and people.
pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.excerptEs: Mapa preliminar: drogas y derivados industriales en el ciclo extraer→desechar — residuos, exceso y daño a plantas, animales y personas.
pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.contentEn:
## Scope

Lab research map: relate **drugs / pharmaceuticals / industrial derivatives** to the **extract → make → sell → discard** cycle and to externalised harm — waste, excess supply, and pressure on **plants, animals and people**.

> **Method note:** independent editorial audit. **Not medical or legal advice.** Does **not** claim a secret «population control» plot. Object = **documentable externalities**. Indexing ≠ endorsement.

## Guiding question

How does the same industrial pattern concentrate profit and shift cost onto ecosystems and bodies — and what can this lab conclude from sheets already published?

## Status

**Preliminary report · ongoing** (`pesquisa-laboratorio`). Step 1: framework + three cases + BudGanja network.

## Weak hypotheses

- H1: Drug, medicine and industrial product share the linear materials chain.  
- H2: Shelf price omits waste, occupational disease and habitat loss.  
- H3: Excess and waste are central mechanisms.  
- H4: Plants, animals and people enter as feedstock, trial subject, consumer or dump — the lab maps links, not genocidal intent.  
- H5: Even medicinal plants enter the map when they become industrial commodities.

## Three anchor cases

1. **Opioids** — culture sheet [The Last Opium Den](/posts/post-inspecao-arte-a-ultima-casa-de-opio.html); scale + weak governance harm people without proving a demographic conspiracy.  
2. **Ultra-processed / free sugars** — [WHO 2015](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-oms-acucares-livres-2015.html), [Hall 2019](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-hall-ultraprocessados-2019.html), sugar/chocolate/gluten sheets.  
3. **Packaging & waste** — Story of Stuff cycle applied to pharma logistics; ecological harm as inventory, not loose metaphor.

## Network

[Story of Stuff](/posts/post-inspecao-arte-a-historia-das-coisas.html) · [Annie Leonard](/posts/post-inspecao-figura-annie-leonard.html) · [Derivatives hub](/biblioteca/inspecoes/#inspecoes-derivados) · [Research hub](/biblioteca/pesquisas/)

## What this does **not** claim

No single committee using substances for population control; no claim that every drug is fraud; no lab effluent measurements in this step.

## Status

**Published — preliminary report** on [Research](/biblioteca/pesquisas/).
pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.contentEs:
## Alcance

Mapa de investigación del laboratorio: relacionar **drogas / fármacos / derivados industriales** con el ciclo **extraer → fabricar → vender → desechar** y con daños externalizados — residuos, exceso de oferta y presión sobre **plantas, animales y personas**.

> **Nota metodológica:** auditoría editorial independiente. **No es consejo médico ni jurídico.** No afirma un plan secreto de «control poblacional». Objeto = **externalidades documentables**. Indexar ≠ respaldar.

## Pregunta guía

¿Cómo el mismo patrón industrial concentra lucro y desplaza costo a ecosistemas y cuerpos — y qué puede concluir el laboratorio con las fichas ya publicadas?

## Estado

**Informe preliminar · en curso** (`pesquisa-laboratorio`). Peldaño 1: marco + tres casos + red BudGanja.

## Hipótesis débiles

- H1: Droga, fármaco y producto industrial comparten la cadena lineal.  
- H2: El precio de estantería omite residuos y pérdida de hábitat.  
- H3: Exagero y desperdicio son mecanismos centrales.  
- H4: Plantas, animales y personas entran como materia prima, ensayo, consumidor o basurero — el lab mapea vínculos, no intención genocida.

## Ver casos y red

[La historia de las cosas](/posts/post-inspecao-arte-a-historia-das-coisas.html) · [Derivados](/biblioteca/inspecoes/#inspecoes-derivados) · [Pesquisas](/biblioteca/pesquisas/)

## Lo que **no** afirma

No hay un comité único de control poblacional; no todo fármaco es fraude; este peldaño no mide efluentes propios.

## Estado

**Publicado — informe preliminar** en [Pesquisas](/biblioteca/pesquisas/).

pesquisa-insumos-organicos-vs-industrial.titleEn: Research: Organic vs industrial inputs — influence on final fruit quality
pesquisa-insumos-organicos-vs-industrial.titleEs: Investigación: Insumos orgánicos vs industrializados — influencia en el fruto final
pesquisa-insumos-organicos-vs-industrial.excerptEn: How organic vs industrial inputs change fruit — and how chemicals cut species links (soil, pollinators, predators), separating us from organic life.
pesquisa-insumos-organicos-vs-industrial.excerptEs: Cómo insumos orgánicos vs industriales cambian el fruto — y cómo las sustancias químicas cortan vínculos entre especies, separándonos de la vida orgánica.
pesquisa-insumos-organicos-vs-industrial.contentEn:
## Scope

Lab research map: compare **organic** vs **industrial** inputs (fertilisers, pesticides, growth regulators, postharvest additives) and their influence on **final fruit quality** — composition, flavour, residues and antioxidants.

> **Method note:** editorial synthesis of published meta-analyses/reviews (2009–2026). **Not agronomic or medical advice.** Dose and management matter as much as the input label.

## Guiding question

What changes in the fruit under slow soil nutrition versus soluble industrial NPK/pesticides/forced ripening — and **how do these substances separate us from organic life across species**?

## Status

**Preliminary report · ongoing** (`pesquisa-laboratorio`). Steps 1–2: fruit quality map + species-separation map.

## Weak hypotheses

- H1: «Organic» alone does not guarantee nutritional superiority on every parameter — **N dose and form** drive much of flavour and phenolics.  
- H2: Excess soluble N diverts carbon to amino acids and lowers sugar/flavonoids/aroma density.  
- H3: Organic systems tend toward higher polyphenols, fewer detectable pesticides and lower cadmium (study averages).  
- H4: Industrial systems tend toward yield and uniformity; typical risks are residues and watery oversized fruit.  
- H5: Postharvest agents (ethylene, ethephon, **calcium carbide**) can ruin quality after a good crop.  
- H6: Keep **fresh fruit** separate from **ultra-processed derivatives** (sugar + additives).  
- H7: Industrial substances **cut species links** (microbe–plant–pollinator–predator–human), replacing living relations with chemical management.

## Species separation (short)

Five typical cuts: living soil → soluble NPK; pest↔predator → insecticide; weeds → herbicide; mycorrhiza → fungicide; shared ripening time → forced gas. Cascades move from field base (plants/invertebrates) up to birds/mammals and outward by drift. The fruit then arrives less «crossed» by other lives.

## Key evidence

- Barański et al. 2014: polyphenols often +19–69% in organic; pesticide detections ~4× higher in conventional; lower Cd on average.  
- Tomato meta-analysis (Wu 2023): organic fertiliser raises soluble sugar, lycopene and vitamin C.  
- Apple multiomics (2021): high N −16% sugar, −19% flavonoids.  
- Strawberry (2024): N form shifts aroma volatiles and phenolics.  
- Reviews 2024–2025: pesticides as biodiversity-erosion drivers via trophic cascades, not only target toxicity.

## Network

[Cherry tomato](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-tomatinho-cereja.html) · [Strawberry](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-morango.html) · [Fruits hub](/biblioteca/inspecoes/#inspecoes-frutos) · [Super Soil guide](/posts/post-guia-calculadora-super-solo.html) · [Molecule to waste](/posts/post-pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.html) · [Research hub](/biblioteca/pesquisas/)

## What this does **not** claim

No claim that every organic fruit is superior on all nutrients; no claim that every industrial fertiliser ruins fruit; no in-house Brix/residue lab in this step.

## Status

**Published — preliminary report** on [Research](/biblioteca/pesquisas/).
pesquisa-insumos-organicos-vs-industrial.contentEs:
## Alcance

Mapa de investigación del laboratorio: comparar insumos **orgánicos** e **industrializados** (fertilizantes, defensivos, reguladores y aditivos poscosecha) y su influencia en la **calidad final del fruto**.

> **Nota metodológica:** síntesis editorial de meta-análisis y revisiones (2009–2026). **No es consejo agronómico ni médico.** La dosis y el manejo pesan tanto como la etiqueta del insumo.

## Pregunta guía

¿Qué cambia en el fruto con nutrición lenta del suelo frente a NPK soluble, pesticidas y maduración forzada — y **de qué forma esas sustancias nos separan de la vida orgánica respecto a las especies**?

## Estado

**Informe preliminar · en curso** (`pesquisa-laboratorio`). Peldaños 1–2: mapa de calidad del fruto + mapa de separación entre especies.

## Hipótesis débiles

- H1: «Orgánico» solo no garantiza superioridad en todos los nutrientes — la **dosis y forma de N** explican gran parte del sabor y los fenólicos.  
- H2: El exceso de N soluble baja azúcar, flavonoides y aroma.  
- H3: Lo orgánico tiende a más polifenoles, menos pesticidas detectables y menos cadmio (promedios de estudios).  
- H4: Lo industrial tiende a más rendimiento; riesgos típicos = residuos y fruto aguado.  
- H5: La poscosecha (etileno, etefón, **carburo de calcio**) puede arruinar el resultado.  
- H6: Separar fruto fresco de derivados ultraprocesados.  
- H7: Las sustancias industriales **cortan vínculos entre especies** (microbio–planta–polinizador–depredador–humano).

## Separación entre especies (breve)

Cinco cortes: suelo vivo → NPK; plaga↔depredador → insecticida; «maleza» → herbicida; micorriza → fungicida; tiempo compartido → gas forzado. La cascada sube desde la base del campo y sale por deriva. El fruto llega menos atravesado por otras vidas.

## Evidencia clave

- Barański 2014: polifenoles a menudo +19–69% en orgánico; pesticidas ~4× más frecuentes en convencional.  
- Tomate (Wu 2023): fertilizante orgánico eleva azúcar, licopeno y vitamina C.  
- Manzana (2021): N alto −16% azúcar, −19% flavonoides.  
- Revisiones 2024–2025: pesticidas como motor de erosión de biodiversidad vía cascadas tróficas.

## Red

[Tomate cherry](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-tomatinho-cereja.html) · [Fresa](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-morango.html) · [Frutos](/biblioteca/inspecoes/#inspecoes-frutos) · [Super Suelo](/posts/post-guia-calculadora-super-solo.html) · [Molécula a la basura](/posts/post-pesquisa-molecula-ao-lixo.html) · [Pesquisas](/biblioteca/pesquisas/)

## Lo que **no** afirma

No todo fruto orgánico es superior en todos los nutrientes; no todo fertilizante industrial arruina el fruto; este peldaño no mide Brix/residuos propios.

## Estado

**Publicado — informe preliminar** en [Pesquisas](/biblioteca/pesquisas/).

pesquisa-oficio-roubo-proibicao.contentEn:
## Scope

Lab research map: relate **craft** (method, gesture, inspection) to **theft / appropriation** and **prohibition / silencing** of the mantra and inspection project — and to the editorial reply **“[Valeu !!!](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-valeu.html)”** (*Valeu !!!*).

> Independent BudGanja audit. **Not legal advice or a named accusation.** Object = the **pattern** (take + silence) and the **method reply**.

## Guiding question

When they steal the phrase (or the work) and still forbid the inspection project, what can the lab document without turning into grudge — and how does “Valeu !!!” work as a map, not an empty slogan?

## Status

**Preliminary report · ongoing** (`pesquisa-laboratorio`). Step 1: framework + three axes + BudGanja network.

## Reading

**H1:** “best” = honest best in this hand, today.  
**H2:** steal + forbid is worse than either alone.  
**H3:** reply is craft, not [revenge](/posts/post-inspecao-expressao-vinganca-mata-alma-envenena.html).  
**H4:** political [prohibition](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-proibicao-proibicionismo.html) and editorial silencing share a verb; they are not the same object.

## Scope

Educational inspection of **Papaya** (*Carica papaya L.*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/plantas/mamao/](/plantas/mamao/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Papaya** |
| Scientific name | *Carica papaya L.* |
| Family | Caricaceae |
| Catalog slug | `mamao` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

Everyday tropical fruit (*Carica papaya*): sweet pulp, seeds and latex with papain — whole fruit vs sugary nectars and industrial snacks; UNIFESP link (papain in wound care).

## Parts used

- Fruit (ripe pulp)
- Seeds (culinary / folk use, with caution)
- Latex / papain (clinical and industrial context — not self-medication)
- Low-process culinary uses

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Fresh fruit (breakfast, dessert, home juice)
- Tropical and Brazilian cooking
- Latex papain cited in SUS wound protocols (UNIFESP training context)
- Family growing in warm climates — fast-growing plant

## Cautions

Ripe pulp is common food. Raw latex can irritate skin and mucosa. Excess seeds and extracts: avoid self-medication. Industrial derivatives with sugar and additives belong in Risk derivatives. Educational content — not professional advice.


## Identity and etymology

Portuguese **mamão** (augmentative of *mama*) names the bulky fruit — common in Brazil; European Portuguese and trade often use **papaya**. **Carica papaya** L. (Caricaceae) from Latin *carica* (fig) and Taíno/Caribbean *papaya*. **Do not** confuse with **castor bean** (*Ricinus communis*) — toxic oil plant, different name.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Papain (latex) | Latex protease — classic marker; cited in SUS wound protocols (UNIFESP training). **Not** a home recipe or self-medication. |
| Carotenoids (β-carotene) | Ripe yellow-orange pulp — pro-vitamin A and colour; educational nutrition interest, not a therapeutic dose. |
| Pulp sugars and fibre | Intact food matrix in fresh fruit — distinct from sweetened industrial nectar/pulp. |
| Seeds (oil / phenolics) | Peppery seeds in the central cavity — occasional culinary tradition; excess and extracts need caution, not home protocols. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh fruit at breakfast | Lab credit line: whole ripe papaya, without «superfood» marketing. |
| Tropical family growing | Fast-growing plant in warm climates — light, drainage and patience; light notes, not an agronomy manual. |
| Papain and living pharmacies (UNIFESP) | Training link: latex → papain in SUS wound care — scientific credit separate from table fruit and self-medication. |
| Fruit vs industry | Nectars, sweetened pulps and «papaya» snacks belong in the Risk Derivatives conversation — like banana and mango. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Ripe pulp is common food. Raw latex irritates skin/mucosa. **Do not** confuse with castor bean (*Ricinus*). Clinical papain/extracts: only with professional guidance. Sugary industrial derivatives belong in Risk Derivatives. Educational BudGanja content.

## Resumen

Fruto tropical cotidiano (*Carica papaya*): pulpa dulce, semillas y látex con papaína — fruto entero vs néctares azucarados y snacks industriales; vínculo UNIFESP (papaína en heridas).

## Partes usadas

- Fruto (pulpa madura)
- Semillas (culinaria / tradición popular, con cautela)
- Látex / papaína (contexto clínico e industrial — no automedicación)
- Uso culinario de bajo procesamiento

## Usos tradicionales (catálogo)

- Consumo del fruto fresco (desayuno, postre, jugo casero)
- Cocina tropical y brasileña
- Papaína del látex citada en protocolos de heridas del SUS (contexto formativo UNIFESP)
- Cultivo familiar en clima cálido — planta de crecimiento rápido

## Cuidados

La pulpa madura es alimento común. El látex crudo puede irritar piel y mucosa. Semillas en exceso y extractos: evitar automedicación. Los derivados industriales con azúcar y aditivos entran en Derivados de riesgo. Contenido educativo — no sustituye orientación profesional.


## Identidad y etimología

El portugués brasileño **mamão** (aumentativo de *mama*) nombra el fruto voluminoso; en comercio internacional predomina **papaya**. **Carica papaya** L. (Caricaceae). **No** confundir con **ricino / mamona** (*Ricinus communis*).

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Papaína (látex) | Proteasa del látex — marcador clásico; citada en protocolos de heridas del SUS. **No** es receta casera ni automedicación. |
| Carotenoides (β-caroteno) | Pulpa madura amarillo-naranja — provitamina A y color; interés nutricional educativo. |
| Azúcares y fibra de la pulpa | Matriz alimentaria intacta en el fruto fresco — distinto de néctar/pulpa industrial endulzada. |
| Semillas (aceite / fenólicos) | Semillas picantes en la cavidad central — tradición culinaria puntual; exceso y extractos piden cautela. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

## Usos y beneficios (contexto educativo)

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |
| --- | --- |
| Fruto fresco en el desayuno | Línea de crédito del laboratorio: papaya entera madura, sin marketing de «superalimento». |
| Cultivo familiar tropical | Planta de crecimiento rápido en clima cálido — luz, drenaje y paciencia; notas ligeras, no manual agronómico. |
| Papaína y farmacias vivas (UNIFESP) | Vínculo formativo: látex → papaína en heridas del SUS — crédito científico separado del fruto de mesa y de la automedicación. |
| Fruto vs industria | Néctares, pulpas endulzadas y snacks «papaya» entran en Derivados de riesgo — como banana y mango. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

Pulpa madura es alimento común. Látex crudo irrita piel/mucosa. **No** confundir con ricino (*Ricinus*). Extractos y papaína clínica: solo con orientación profesional. Derivados industriales azucarados entran en Derivados de riesgo.

## Scope

Educational inspection of **Watermelon** (*Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

| Field | Value |

| Common name | **Watermelon** |
| Scientific name | *Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai* |
| Family | Cucurbitaceae |
| Catalog slug | `melancia` |
| Inspection date | 2026-07-31 |

## Summary

Summer cucurbit (*Citrullus lanatus*): refreshing watery pulp — this sheet separates whole watermelon from juices, nectars and ultra-processed «watermelon»; market, beach and light home-grow culture.

## Parts used

- Fruit (fresh pulp)
- Seeds (toasted / traditional cooking, in moderation)
- Low-process culinary uses (homemade juice, salad)

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Fresh fruit (summer, market, beach)
- Homemade juice and salad without ultra-processing
- Food culture of watermelon
- Family growing in warm climates — vine with space and pollination

## Cautions

Ripe pulp is common food — natural fruit sugar counts in daily dose. Excess seeds and extracts: no self-medication. Green plant parts are not the food focus of this sheet. Industrial derivatives with sugar/syrups/additives belong in Risk derivatives. Educational — not professional advice.


## Identity and etymology

Portuguese **melancia** (also **melão-d'água**) ties to the **melon** family (*melo* / *melão*) — a large sweet summer fruit. Binomial **Citrullus lanatus** (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai (**Cucurbitaceae**): *Citrullus* names the citrullus group; *lanatus* = «woolly», for pubescent young leaves/stems. English *watermelon*; Spanish *sandía*. **Do not** confuse with melon (*Cucumis melo*) — distinct species, same table culture.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Pulp water and electrolytes | Ripe pulp ~90% water — summer hydrating matrix; potassium and natural sugars in whole-fruit dose. |
| Citrulline | Non-essential amino acid — name tied to *Citrullus*; in pulp and especially the white rind. Educational nutrition interest, **not** a gym dose. |
| Lycopene (red pulp) | Carotenoid of ripe red pulp — colour and lipophilic antioxidant; yellow cultivars have a different pigment profile. |
| Seeds (oil / protein) | Toasted seeds — occasional culinary tradition; excess and extracts need moderation, not home protocols. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh summer fruit (market / beach) | Lab credit line: whole chilled watermelon, without «detox» marketing — Brazilian table-and-shade culture. |
| Homemade juice and salad | Low processing — distinct from nectar, soft drinks and «watermelon» snacks with sugar and flavours. |
| Family growing (light notes) | Warm-climate vine: sun, ground space or trellis, regular water and bees at flowering — patience, not an agronomy manual. |
| Fruit vs industry | Concentrate juices, nectars and ultra-processed «watermelon» belong in Risk Derivatives — cross free sugars / sugarcane. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Ripe pulp is common food — natural sugar counts in dose. Seeds and extracts: no self-medication. **Do not** confuse with melon (*Cucumis melo*). Sugary industrial derivatives belong in Risk Derivatives. Educational BudGanja content.

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

Pulpa madura es alimento común — el azúcar natural cuenta. Semillas y extractos: sin automedicación. **No** confundir con melón (*Cucumis melo*). Derivados industriales azucarados entran en Derivados de riesgo.

pesquisa-fitocanabinoides.contentEn:
## Scope

BudGanja lab catalogue of **phytocannabinoids** — plant molecules (mainly *Cannabis sativa*) that meet the [endocannabinoidome](/posts/post-inspecao-neurociencia-endocanabinoidoma.html). Complements the [chemotype guide](/posts/post-inspecao-guia-quimiotipos-cannabis.html) and [XIV Lesson 10](/biblioteca/unifesp/livro-xiv.html#aula-10).

> **Not medical advice, HPLC report, extraction protocol, dose or grow guide.**

## Three families

| Family | Origin | Example |
|--------|--------|---------|
| Phytocannabinoids | Plant trichomes | THCA, CBD, CBG |
| Endocannabinoids | Body | Anandamide, 2-AG |
| Synthetics | Human lab | Licensed drugs **or** illicit CB1 agonists — **no synthesis recipes** |

## Biosynthesis (textbook, not bench)

Olivetolic acid + GPP → **CBGA** (mother node) → THCA / CBDA / CBCA via plant enzymes. Heat/light/time **decarboxylate** acids to neutrals. THC oxidises toward **CBN**. Propyl (varin) series from divarinolic acid: THCV, CBDV.

## Catalogue (axes)

- **CBG/CBGA** — biosynthetic mother; chemotype 4.  
- **Δ9-THC/THCA** — partial CB1 agonist; developmental caution ([Albaugh](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-albaugh-cannabis-neurodesenvolvimento.html)); potency × first-episode psychosis ([Di Forti](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-diforti-eugei-psicose-2019.html)).  
- **CBD/CBDA** — low CB1 affinity; strongest human signal in rare epilepsies ([Devinsky](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-devinsky-cbd-dravet-2017.html) RCT); isolate ≠ whole plant.  
- **CBC** — minor chromene.  
- **CBN** — aged THC; sleep marketing outruns evidence.  
- **THCV / CBDV** — C3 varins; not diet drops.  
- **Δ8 / HHC / THC-O** — mostly **not** the living-plant catalogue.

## Chemotypes 1–5

See [chemotype guide](/posts/post-inspecao-guia-quimiotipos-cannabis.html): THC-dominant → balanced → CBD → CBG → fiber (negligible cannabinoids).

## Status

**Published — catalogue step 1** on [Research](/biblioteca/pesquisas/).

[▶ Chemotypes](/posts/post-inspecao-guia-quimiotipos-cannabis.html) · [▶ Endocannabinoidome](/posts/post-inspecao-neurociencia-endocanabinoidoma.html) · [▶ Plant](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-cannabis-sativa.html)
pesquisa-fitocanabinoides.contentEs:
## Alcance

Catálogo de laboratorio de **fitocannabinoides** — moléculas de planta (sobre todo *Cannabis sativa*) que cruzan el [endocannabinoidoma](/posts/post-inspecao-neurociencia-endocanabinoidoma.html). Complementa la [guía de quimiotipos](/posts/post-inspecao-guia-quimiotipos-cannabis.html) y la [Aula 10 del XIV](/biblioteca/unifesp/livro-xiv.html#aula-10).

> **No es consejo médico, laudo HPLC, protocolo de extracción, dosis ni cultivo.**

## Tres familias

Fitocannabinoides (planta) · endocannabinoides (cuerpo) · sintéticos (laboratorio humano: fármaco registrado **o** agonistas ilícitos — **sin recetas de síntesis**).

## Biosíntesis (libro, no bancada)

Ácido olivetólico + GPP → **CBGA** (nodo madre) → THCA / CBDA / CBCA. Calor/luz/tiempo **descarboxilan**. El THC oxida hacia **CBN**. Serie varin (C3): THCV, CBDV.

## Catálogo (ejes)

CBG/CBGA · Δ9-THC/THCA (cautela en desarrollo, [Albaugh](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-albaugh-cannabis-neurodesenvolvimento.html); potencia × psicosis, [Di Forti](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-diforti-eugei-psicose-2019.html)) · CBD/CBDA (epilepsias raras, [Devinsky](/posts/post-inspecao-artigo-devinsky-cbd-dravet-2017.html); aislado ≠ planta) · CBC · CBN (marketing de sueño adelanta la evidencia) · THCV/CBDV · Δ8/HHC fuera del catálogo de la planta viva.

## Quimiotipos 1–5

Ver [guía](/posts/post-inspecao-guia-quimiotipos-cannabis.html).

## Estado

**Publicado — catálogo peldaño 1** en [Pesquisas](/biblioteca/pesquisas/).

## Scope

Educational inspection of **Psilocybe cubensis** (*Psilocybe cubensis (Earle) Singer*) from the Inspetor BudGanja **fungi** catalog. This report restates the public sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol, **not** a cultivation guide and **does not replace** professional advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/fungos/psilocybe-cubensis/](/fungos/psilocybe-cubensis/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Psilocybe cubensis** |
| Scientific name | *Psilocybe cubensis (Earle) Singer* |
| Family | Hymenogastraceae |
| Kingdom | Fungi |
| Catalog slug | `psilocybe-cubensis` |
| Inspection date | 2026-08-19 |

## Summary

*Psilocybe cubensis* — the cosmopolitan *Psilocybe* most cited in contemporary outreach; in UNIFESP XIV it is named as a psychedelic fungus of craft, distinct from classic Mazatec species. Identification and framing sheet — not a grow guide or a dose.

## Parts / characters of office

- Basidioma (cap + stipe) — object of mycological identification
- Purple-dark spore print — diagnostic character (not a recipe)
- Psilocybin / psilocin — named on the map, no extraction

## Traditional and formative context (catalog)

- Named in UNIFESP XIV alongside *Psilocybe caerulescens* as an example of a psychedelic fungus
- Type-species of contemporary “magic mushroom” outreach — distinct from classic Mazatec species (*P. mexicana* and kin)
- Object of ethnomycology and public psychopharmacology — indexing ≠ endorsing use

## Cautions

Psilocybin and psilocin are controlled in Brazil (SVS/MS Ordinance 344/1998 and updates — check current lists). Sheet ≠ cultivation, dose, extraction or use protocol. Confusion with *Galerina* and other toxic basidiomata can be fatal — field ID needs an expert. Does not replace a physician, pharmacist, mycologist or lawyer.

## Craft identification (not a field protocol)

Purple-dark spore print and bluing are diagnostic characters of office. Golden cap ≠ closed ID. *Galerina* and other toxic basidiomata kill. Field ID is expert work.

## What this sheet is **not**

Cultivation protocol, substrate, spores, fruiting, kit, dose table, extraction, or a licence to possess or use.

## Named chemistry (map, not bench)

Psilocybin → psilocin; 5-HT2A class in the literature. Naming ≠ synthesis. See [alucinógeno](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-alucinogeno.html) vs the [endocannabinoidome](/posts/post-inspecao-neurociencia-endocanabinoidoma.html).

## Brazilian law (framing, not legal advice)

Psilocybin and psilocin appear on [ANVISA](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-anvisa.html) lists (Ordinance 344/1998 and updates — **check the current text**).

## UNIFESP XIV

The psychedelics lesson names **Psilocybe cubensis** and **Psilocybe caerulescens**. Classic Mazatec species are mostly others (*P. mexicana* and kin).

## Valeu !!!

Best possible **when naming the fungus without turning it into a grow**, today.


## UNIFESP link

This species is marked as related to the lab's UNIFESP extension track. See the [UNIFESP hub](/biblioteca/unifesp/) and the [course inspection](/posts/post-inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicinal.html).

## Resumen

*Psilocybe cubensis* — la especie cosmopolita de *Psilocybe* más citada en la divulgación contemporánea; en el XIV UNIFESP entra como hongo psicodélico de oficio, distinta de las especies mazatecas clásicas. Ficha de identificación y encuadre — no es cultivo ni dosis.

## Partes / caracteres de oficio

- Basidioma (sombrero + estípite) — objeto de identificación micológica
- Esporada púrpura-oscura — carácter diagnóstico (no es receta)
- Psilocibina / psilocina — sustancias nombradas en el mapa, sin extracción

## Contexto tradicional y formativo (catálogo)

- Nombrada en el XIV UNIFESP junto a *Psilocybe caerulescens* como ejemplo de hongo psicodélico
- Especie-tipo de la divulgación contemporánea de «hongos mágicos» — distinta de las especies mazatecas clásicas (*P. mexicana* y afines)
- Objeto de etnomícología y psicofarmacología pública — catalogar ≠ respaldar uso

## Cuidados

Psilocibina y psilocina están controladas en Brasil (Portaria SVS/MS 344/1998 y actualizaciones — conferir listas vigentes). Ficha ≠ protocolo de cultivo, dosis, extracción o uso. Confusión con *Galerina* y otros basidiomas tóxicos puede ser fatal — la identificación de campo exige perito. No sustituye médico, farmacéutico, micólogo ni abogado.

## Identificación de oficio (no es protocolo de campo)

Esporada púrpura-oscura y azulado son caracteres diagnósticos. Sombrero dorado ≠ identificación cerrada. *Galerina* y otros basidiomas tóxicos matan. La ID de campo es trabajo de perito.

## Lo que esta ficha **no** es

Protocolo de cultivo, sustrato, esporas, fructificación, kit, tabla de dosis, extracción ni autorización de uso.

## Química nombrada (mapa, no bancada)

Psilocibina → psilocina; clase 5-HT2A en la literatura. Nombrar ≠ sintetizar. Ver [alucinógeno](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-alucinogeno.html) y el [endocannabinoidoma](/posts/post-inspecao-neurociencia-endocanabinoidoma.html).

## Derecho brasileño (encuadre, no dictamen)

Psilocibina y psilocina constan en listas de [ANVISA](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-anvisa.html) (Portaria 344/1998 y actualizaciones — **conferir el texto vigente**).

## XIV UNIFESP

La clase de psicodélicos nombra **Psilocybe cubensis** y **Psilocybe caerulescens**. Las especies mazatecas clásicas son sobre todo otras (*P. mexicana* y afines).

## ¡Valeu !!!

Lo mejor posible **al nombrar el hongo sin convertirlo en cultivo**, hoy.


## Vínculo UNIFESP

Esta especie está marcada como relacionada con el eje de extensión UNIFESP del laboratorio. Ver el [hub UNIFESP](/biblioteca/unifesp/) y la [inspección del curso](/posts/post-inspecao-curso-unifesp-cannabis-medicinal.html).

inspecao-planta-alecrim-do-campo.contentEn:
## Scope

Educational inspection of **Field rosemary (alecrim-do-campo)** (*Baccharis dracunculifolia DC.*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/plantas/alecrim-do-campo/](/plantas/alecrim-do-campo/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Field rosemary (alecrim-do-campo)** |
| Scientific name | *Baccharis dracunculifolia DC.* |
| Family | Asteraceae |
| Catalog slug | `alecrim-do-campo` |
| Inspection date | 2026-08-21 |

## Summary

Cerrado native shrub (*Baccharis dracunculifolia*) — golden rosemary / vassourinha; botanical source of Brazilian green propolis (artepillin C). Do not confuse with kitchen rosemary (*Salvia rosmarinus*).

## Parts used

- Leaves and vegetative apices (traditional infusion)
- Flowers / golden inflorescences
- Bud resin (collected by bees → green propolis)

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Folk infusion of leaves and flowers (cultural craft, not clinical posology)
- Digestive, respiratory and antiseptic-rinse tradition
- Botanical source of Brazilian green propolis (*Apis mellifera*)
- Pioneer species in restoring degraded land (ecological context)

## Cautions

Contraindicated in pregnancy and nursing. Not recommended under age 12. People on hypoglycemics: monitor glucose — tea does not replace medicine. Avoid excessive or prolonged use without guidance. Do not confuse with kitchen rosemary (*Salvia rosmarinus*) or carqueja (*Baccharis trimera*). Educational — avoid self-medication.


## Identity and etymology

**Field rosemary**, **golden rosemary** and **vassourinha** name *Baccharis dracunculifolia* DC. (Asteraceae) — a South American shrub common in the Cerrado. The epithet *dracunculifolia* describes the narrow leaf. **Not** kitchen [rosemary](/plantas/alecrim/) (*Salvia rosmarinus*, Lamiaceae). Mature twigs dry and brittle; bright-green lanceolate leaves, toothed on young shoots; petal-less golden inflorescences. Same genus as [carqueja](/plantas/carqueja/) (*B. trimera*), a different species.

Field photo by Inspetor BudGanja (21 August 2026) — dense garden shrub with packed narrow leaves:

![Field rosemary in situ — Inspetor BudGanja, 21 August 2026](/imagens/plantas/alecrim-do-campo-campo.jpg)

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Artepillin C (3,5-diprenyl-p-coumaric acid) | Prenylated phenolic marker of buds and Brazilian green propolis — the most cited chemical link between the plant and the bee product. |
| Baccharin and drupanin | Congener prenylated p-coumaric acids — profile shared by vegetative apices and green propolis. |
| Flavonoids (naringenin, isosakuranetin, kaempferide) | Aerial parts and propolis — phenolic contribution beyond prenylated acids. |
| Essential oil ((E)-nerolidol, spathulenol) | Volatile fraction of leaves and shoots; nerolidol is the most cited constituent of the aromatic fraction. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Botanical source of green propolis | *Apis mellifera* collects resin from buds and apices — the bee product concentrates plant markers (artepillin C). Link to the [honeybee](/animais/abelha/) sheet. This is **not** a supplement endorsement. |
| Traditional infusion (leaves and flowers) | Folk guides describe a short infusion of dried leaves/flowers after the boil (heat off). The lab treats this as **cultural craft**, not clinical posology or diabetes treatment. |
| Digestive, respiratory and topical tradition | Folk use in dyspepsia/gas, airways and antiseptic rinses. Scientific interest (anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial in models) **does not** replace diagnosis or medicine. |
| Glycemic interest (not a treatment) | Phenolics studied in glycemic models — **do not** replace metformin or other hypoglycemics. Hypoglycemia risk if combined with drug. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

**Contraindicated** in pregnancy and nursing (emmenagogue tradition; uterine-contraction risk cited in safety guides). Not recommended under age 12. People on hypoglycemics: monitor glucose — tea is **not** therapy. Avoid excessive or prolonged use without guidance. Distinguish from [carqueja](/plantas/carqueja/) and [rosemary](/plantas/alecrim/). Educational — avoid self-medication.

## Links in the lab

- [Inspection: Kitchen rosemary (*Salvia rosmarinus*) — do not confuse](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-alecrim.html)
- [Inspection: Carqueja (*Baccharis trimera*) — same genus](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-carqueja.html)
- [Inspection: Honeybee — propolis, honey and hive chain](/posts/post-inspecao-animal-abelha.html)
- [Inspection: Bee derivatives — adulterated honey vs propolis](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-abelha.html)

inspecao-planta-alecrim-do-campo.contentEs:
## Alcance

Inspección educativa de **Alecrim-do-campo (romero de campo)** (*Baccharis dracunculifolia DC.*) del catálogo de plantas medicinales del Inspetor BudGanja. Este informe reúne la ficha pública con método verificable del laboratorio — **no** es un protocolo clínico y **no sustituye** orientación profesional de salud.

> **Nota metodológica:** auditoría independiente BudGanja a partir de la ficha en [/plantas/alecrim-do-campo/](/plantas/alecrim-do-campo/). Solo contenido educativo.

## Objeto inspeccionado

| Campo | Valor |
|-------|-------|
| Nombre popular | **Alecrim-do-campo (romero de campo)** |
| Nombre científico | *Baccharis dracunculifolia DC.* |
| Familia | Asteraceae |
| Slug del catálogo | `alecrim-do-campo` |
| Fecha de inspección | 2026-08-21 |

## Resumen

Arbusto nativo del Cerrado (*Baccharis dracunculifolia*) — romero dorado / vassourinha; fuente botánica del propóleo verde brasileño (artepilina C). No confundir con el romero de cocina (*Salvia rosmarinus*).

## Partes usadas

- Hojas y ápices vegetativos (infusión tradicional)
- Flores / inflorescencias amarillo-oro
- Resina de brotes (cosecha por abejas → propóleo verde)

## Usos tradicionales (catálogo)

- Infusión popular de hojas y flores (oficio cultural, no posología clínica)
- Tradición digestiva, respiratoria y de enjuagues antisépticos
- Fuente botánica del propóleo verde brasileño (*Apis mellifera*)
- Especie pionera en recuperación de áreas degradadas (contexto ecológico)

## Cuidados

Contraindicado en embarazo y lactancia. No recomendado menores de 12 años. Diabéticos con hipoglucemiantes: monitorizar glucosa — el té no sustituye fármaco. Evitar uso excesivo o prolongado sin orientación. No confundir con romero de cocina (*Salvia rosmarinus*) ni carqueja (*Baccharis trimera*). Contenido educativo — evite automedicación.


## Identidad y etimología

**Alecrim-do-campo**, **alecrim dourado** y **vassourinha** nombran *Baccharis dracunculifolia* DC. (Asteraceae) — arbusto nativo de Sudamérica, frecuente en el Cerrado. El epíteto *dracunculifolia* describe la hoja estrecha. **No es** el [romero de cocina](/plantas/alecrim/) (*Salvia rosmarinus*, Lamiaceae). Ramas maduras secas y quebradizas; hojas lanceoladas verde brillante, dentadas en brotes; inflorescencias amarillo-oro sin pétalos. Mismo género que la [carqueja](/plantas/carqueja/) (*B. trimera*), especie distinta.

Foto de campo del Inspetor BudGanja (21 de agosto de 2026) — arbusto denso de jardín, hojas estrechas:

![Alecrim-do-campo en campo — Inspetor BudGanja, 21 de agosto de 2026](/imagens/plantas/alecrim-do-campo-campo.jpg)

## Química y marcadores

| Marcador | Notas |
| --- | --- |
| Artepilina C (ácido 3,5-diprenil-p-cumárico) | Marcador fenólico prenilado de yemas y del propóleo verde brasileño — el vínculo químico más citado entre la planta y el producto de las abejas. |
| Baccharina y drupanina | Ácidos p-cumáricos prenilados congéneres — perfil compartido entre ápices vegetativos y propóleo verde. |
| Flavonoides (naringenina, isosakuraneetina, kaempferídeo) | Partes aéreas y propóleo — contribución fenólica además de los ácidos prenilados. |
| Aceite esencial ((E)-nerolidol, espatulenol) | Fracción volátil de hojas y brotes; el nerolidol es el constituyente más citado de la fracción aromática. |

**Límites de la lectura química:** los perfiles varían según cultivar, parte usada, secado y preparación. Esto **no** es protocolo clínico ni análisis de producto.

## Usos y beneficios (contexto educativo)

| Tema | Cómo lo enmarca el laboratorio |
| --- | --- |
| Fuente botánica del propóleo verde | *Apis mellifera* recolecta resina de brotes y ápices — el producto de las abejas concentra marcadores de la planta (artepilina C). Vínculo con la ficha de la [abeja](/animais/abelha/). Esto **no** es endoso de suplemento. |
| Infusión tradicional (hojas y flores) | Guías populares describen infusión corta de hojas/flores secas tras el hervor (fuego apagado). El laboratorio lo trata como **oficio cultural**, no como posología clínica ni tratamiento de diabetes. |
| Tradición digestiva, respiratoria y tópica | Uso popular en dispepsia/gases, vías respiratorias y enjuagues antisépticos. El interés científico **no** sustituye diagnóstico ni fármaco. |
| Interés glucémico (no es tratamiento) | Fenólicos estudiados en modelos de glucemia — **no** sustituyen metformina ni otro hipoglucemiante. Riesgo de hipoglucemia si se combina con fármaco. |

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

**Contraindicado** en embarazo y lactancia (tradición emenagoga). No recomendado menores de 12 años. Diabéticos con hipoglucemiantes: monitorizar glucosa — el té **no** es terapéutica. Evitar uso excesivo o prolongado sin orientación. Distinguir de [carqueja](/plantas/carqueja/) y [romero](/plantas/alecrim/). Contenido educativo — evite automedicación.

inspecao-planta-marolo.contentEn:
## Scope

Educational inspection of **Marolo** (*Annona crassiflora Mart.*) from the Inspetor BudGanja medicinal plants catalog. This report restates the public plant sheet with a verifiable lab method — it is **not** a clinical protocol and **does not replace** professional health advice.

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit based on the catalog entry at [/plantas/marolo/](/plantas/marolo/). Educational content only.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Common name | **Marolo** |
| Scientific name | *Annona crassiflora Mart.* |
| Family | Annonaceae |
| Catalog slug | `marolo` |
| Inspection date | 2026-08-23 |

## Summary

Anonácea nativa do Cerrado (*Annona crassiflora*): marolo / araticum-do-cerrado — polpa cremosa, muitas sementes; a ficha separa o fruto inteiro de maracujá, mamão, pinha/ata e graviola, e dos néctares e doces industriais.

## Parts used

- Fruto (polpa fresca madura)
- Preparações culinárias de baixo processamento (doce, suco, sorvete caseiros)

## Traditional uses (catalog)

- Consumo da polpa madura (feira, quintal, Cerrado / Minas Gerais)
- Doces e sucos caseiros sem ultraprocessamento
- Cultura alimentar do araticum / marolo no bioma Cerrado

## Cautions

Polpa madura é alimento tradicional. Sementes e folhas de Annonaceae não são chá genérico nem extracto caseiro. Não confundir com maracujá, mamão, pinha/ata ou graviola. Derivados industriais com açúcar entram na série Derivados de risco. Conteúdo educacional — não substitui orientação profissional nem manejo do bioma.


## Identity and etymology

Field request: **Fruto Marolo**. Two rooms: the word [fruto](/posts/post-inspecao-palavra-fruto.html) (*fructus*) and **this** species. **Marolo** is the living name especially in Minas Gerais; **araticum** comes from Old Tupi *aratiku* — a name for several Annonaceae, not one binomial. The lab anchors on **Annona crassiflora** Mart. (**Annonaceae**): *crassiflora* = “thick-flowered”. **Do not** fuse with [passion fruit](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-maracuja-fruta.html), [papaya](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-mamao.html), sugar-apple (*Annona squamosa*) or soursop (*A. muricata*). Regional nicknames do **not** change the binomial.

## Chemistry and markers

| Marker | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Pulp (water, sugars, fiber) | Cream-yellow pulp when ripe — Cerrado food matrix; strong aroma; natural sugar in fruit dose, not industrial nectar. |
| Numerous seeds | The fruit carries many dark seeds — eat the **pulp**, not the pit as “tea”. Annonaceae seed ≠ table food. |
| Acetogenins (Annonaceae family) | Family markers, especially in seed/leaf — educational phytochemical interest. **Not** an extract recipe or “pit tea” protocol. |
| Carotenoids / vitamin C (pulp) | Nutritional interest of fresh pulp — varies with ripeness and batch; not a therapeutic dose. |

**Limits of chemical readout:** profiles vary by cultivar, plant part, drying and preparation. This is **not** a clinical protocol or product assay.

## Uses and benefits (educational context)

| Theme | How the lab frames it |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh fruit (Cerrado / MG) | Credit line: ripe pulp at table, market and yard — Minas and Cerrado culture, without superfood marketing. |
| Home sweet, juice and liqueur | Low processing — distinct from sweetened pulps, nectars and industrial liqueurs with sugar and flavouring. |
| Native tree (light notes) | Marolo tree: slow growth, Cerrado, fleshy flowers. Patience and respect for the biome — not a forestry or extraction manual. |
| Fruit vs industry / vs leaf tea | Sweetened nectar and pulp = Derivatives conversation. Annonaceae leaf and seed **do not** become a protocol in this sheet. |

**Limits of evidence:** folk tradition and scientific interest **do not** replace diagnosis, prescription or professional care.

## Reinforced cautions

Ripe pulp is traditional Cerrado food. Annonaceae seeds and leaves are not a “generic tea”: family acetogenins ask for respect, not a home extract. Do not confuse with papaya, passion fruit, sugar-apple or soursop. Sugary derivatives belong in Risk Derivatives. Educational — not professional advice or biome management.

**Límites de la evidencia:** la tradición popular y el interés científico **no** sustituyen diagnóstico, prescripción ni seguimiento profesional.

## Cuidados reforzados

inspecao-derivado-laranja.excerptEn: Risk derivatives: from whole orange to ultra-processed Reconstituted juice, nectar, orange soft drinks, jelly, flavour and colours — chemical map of free sugars + additives, cross-linked to the plant sheet and sugarcane.

inspecao-derivado-laranja.contentEn:
## Scope

Editorial and **chemical** inspection of **industrial Orange derivatives** (*Citrus × sinensis (L.) Osbeck*) — credit the whole fruit, audit **Reconstituted juice, nectar, orange soft drinks, jelly, flavour and colours**. Cross-links: [plant sheet](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-laranja.html), [Sugarcane / free sugars](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html).

> **Method note:** independent BudGanja audit. Starting points: plant catalog, Wikipedia, WHO free sugars / ultra-processed debate, Anvisa additives framing. **Not medical advice.** Not a brand lab test. Plant ≠ villain; focus is **transformed food matrix**.

Néctar e refrigerante **não** são o sumo da fruta. No rótulo, procurar **% de suco**.

## Inspected object

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Origin plant | Orange — [plant inspection](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-laranja.html) |
| BudGanja type | Risk derivative — fruit → industrial product |
| Focus | Reconstituted juice, nectar, orange soft drinks, jelly, flavour and colours |
| Chemical focus | Free sugars + additives |
| Date | 2026-08-24 |

## Hypotheses

**H1:** whole fruit ≠ ultra-processed “orange” marketing matrix.  
**H2:** risk axis = **sugar + energy density + formulation additives + frequency**.  
**H3:** label literacy is the repeatable tool.

## Chemistry map (summary)

| Stage | What it is | Editorial note |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| Fruto inteiro (gomos) | Alimento | Fibra, C, hesperidina; dose = peça inteira |
| Sumo fresco espremido | Baixo processamento | Perde fibra; açúcares do fruto ficam livres |
| Suco de concentrado | Reconstituição industrial | Água + concentrado ± açúcar ± aromas |
| Néctar «de laranja» | Bebida adoçada | Pouca fruta + muita água + açúcar — ler % |
| Refrigerante / aroma | Ultraprocessado | Aroma e corante podem substituir a fruta |

Baseline: Vitamina C, flavonoides (hesperidina), fibra no fruto inteiro; o suco perde o bagaço

Industrial add-ons: Concentrado + água + açúcar/xarope + acidulantes + aromas + conservantes ± corantes — sugar / HFCS / maltodextrin · citric/ascorbic acids · sorbate/benzoate · flavours/colours · thickeners. Cross [sugarcane](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html).

## Health framing

WHO free-sugars limits; don’t swap whole fruit for “flavour” snacks. **Editorial verdict:** credit the fruit; alert on sugary additive-laden derivatives.

## Status

**Approved in Risk derivatives.**

[▶ Derivatives](/biblioteca/inspecoes/#inspecoes-derivados) · [▶ Plant](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-laranja.html) · [▶ Sugarcane](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html)
inspecao-derivado-laranja.contentEs:
## Alcance

Inspección editorial y **química** de **derivados industriales de Naranja** (*Citrus × sinensis (L.) Osbeck*) — rescatar el fruto entero y auditar **Jugo reconstituido, néctar, refresco «de naranja», jalea, aroma y colorantes**. Cruces: [planta](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-laranja.html), [caña / azúcares libres](/posts/post-inspecao-derivado-cana-de-acucar.html).

> **Nota metodológica:** auditoría independiente. No es consejo médico ni análisis de una marca. La planta no es el villano; el foco es la **matriz transformada**.

Néctar e refrigerante **não** são o sumo da fruta. No rótulo, procurar **% de suco**.

## Objeto

| Campo | Valor |
|-------|-------|
| Planta | Naranja — [inspección planta](/posts/post-inspecao-planta-laranja.html) |
| Tipo | Derivado de riesgo |
| Foco | Jugo reconstituido, néctar, refresco «de naranja», jalea, aroma y colorantes |
| Química | Azúcares libres + aditivos |
